labels.mechanism: Style cache key joins property and resource key with unescaped | and =, so distinct ThemeRef maps (e.g. Background 'A|Foreground=B' vs Background 'A' + Foreground 'B') collide on one cached Style; quoting added in the same change makes such keys parse.
labels.required_evidence: Identify BuildCacheKey's unescaped delimiter join and a concrete colliding pair or collision consequence.

labels.mechanism: When every ThemeRef key is unrepresentable, the setters.Length == 0 early return leaves the previous render's themed Style installed, so the old brush persists.
labels.required_evidence: Identify the empty-setters early return and that the prior Style is not cleared/restored.

labels.mechanism: GetExactStyleTargetType maps a custom/derived control to its first WinUI ancestor type; BasedOn the author's Style then fails and TryApplyBasedStyle restores the author Style, dropping the ThemeRefs.
labels.required_evidence: Identify the ancestor-type target selection and the resulting BasedOn/TargetType mismatch that discards ThemeRefs.

labels.mechanism: ClearForClickAway sets _suppressCaret = true and only focus change or press clears it; a click-away onto a non-focusable target leaves arrow keys moving an invisible caret.
labels.required_evidence: Identify the suppress flag set on click-away and the missing reset path for non-focusable targets.

labels.mechanism: The click-away handler clears the selection for presses on the ScrollViewer scrollbar (no owning host), so scrolling to finish a selection loses it.
labels.required_evidence: Identify that scrollbar presses are treated as click-away and clear selection.

labels.mechanism: The Shift+drag anchor is stored relative to the pressed surface and clamped into it on rebuild, so a mid-drag document change makes the anchor jump.
labels.required_evidence: Identify the surface-relative anchor storage/clamping and the document-change consequence.

labels.mechanism: Refresh() calls _clicks.Reset() whenever the document changed, and OnPressed refreshes before _clicks.Press, so while content streams the click count never exceeds 1 and double/triple-click breaks.
labels.required_evidence: Identify the Reset in Refresh ordering before Press and the multi-click consequence during document changes.

labels.mechanism: If focus is outside the repeater when the post-reorder check runs, it returns without installing a watch; a shifted stale row focused later stays stale and pinned.
labels.required_evidence: Identify the early return when focus is outside and the later-focus consequence.

labels.mechanism: If no candidate row accepts focus (only focusable row removed, list cleared), the method exits with the stale control still focused and pinned; no fallback.
labels.required_evidence: Identify the no-candidate exit path leaving the stale control focused/pinned.

labels.mechanism: Off-screen/clipped rows are only sorted last rather than excluded, so when no visible row takes focus an off-screen row receives focus and the list scroll-jumps.
labels.required_evidence: Identify that off-viewport candidates remain eligible and the scroll-into-view consequence.

labels.mechanism: The index-collision exemption also spares a key that was removed from the list, leaving its stale control pinned.
labels.required_evidence: Identify the exemption logic not distinguishing removed keys.

labels.mechanism: A correctly placed row after a multi-position move is treated as stale and loses focus.
labels.required_evidence: Identify the staleness test misclassifying a correctly placed row after multi-position moves.

labels.mechanism: Calling Focus() to move focus off a stale row can activate an inactive window.
labels.required_evidence: Identify the unconditional Focus() call and window-activation side effect.

labels.mechanism: The LayoutUpdated handler armed for off-tree or collapsed elements is never detached on cancel or unmount, retaining the control and composition state until a later layout pass.
labels.required_evidence: Identify the LayoutUpdated subscription and missing detach on cancel/unmount.

labels.mechanism: The recovery check uses TryGetAnimationController("Opacity") is not null, which does not see an ExpressionAnimation; ApplyScrollAnimation runs after the check is armed without cancelling it, so recovery replaces a .ScrollLinked opacity expression with the keyframe.
labels.required_evidence: Identify the controller check blind to ExpressionAnimation and the scroll-linked opacity overwrite.

findings.title: Duplicate-key fallback can paint the first item into the last item's control
findings.evidence: ReactorListState.Reset preserves duplicate keys in Source and makes ByKey point to the first occurrence. GetElement overwrites _controlByKey[key] with the last control realized for that key. If two visible rows share a key but have different button labels, a content-only refresh now builds the first row's label from ByKey and writes it into the second row's control. The old index lookup targeted the first row. This breaks the existing duplicate-key recovery path even without a reorder.
findings.recommendation: Give each occurrence a distinct internal realization identity in the duplicate-key fallback. Keep the author key for diagnostics, but pair each control with its own row and previous Element when refreshing.

findings.title: Moving a row across several positions can steal focus from a correctly displayed row
findings.evidence: The check treats another control claiming the same native index as the only proof that a focused row is still displayed correctly. On a move from [A,B,C,D] to [D,A,B,C], B can remain correctly displayed at slot 2 with native index 1. No other control has to claim native index 1, so the check sends focus away from B even though it never entered the pinned pool.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish a parked or wrongly displayed control from a correctly arranged survivor using layout evidence rather than index collisions alone. Add a live test that keeps focus on an intermediate shifted row during a multi-position move.

findings.title: A row focused after a reorder can still be pinned under its old index
findings.evidence: The collection-change check unsubscribes before looking for the focused child. If focus is outside the repeater during that pass, it returns without installing a viewport watcher. A user can then tab into a shifted row and scroll it away without another collection change. Its native index is still stale, but neither focus acquisition nor scrolling that row schedules a check, leaving the original wrong-row reuse path open.
findings.recommendation: While stale native indices remain possible, observe focus entering or changing rows and arm the viewport check for the newly focused child. Cancel that tracking when the child is recycled or the repeater is detached.

findings.title: A stale control stays pinned if no remaining row can take focus
findings.evidence: The only recovery attempts focus on other realized rows. If the removed offscreen row held the list's only focusable control and the remaining rows are text-only, every attempt fails. The one-shot check has already unsubscribed, so the stale control can remain pinned and be returned at its old index when the user scrolls back.
findings.recommendation: Provide a focus fallback outside the stale row, such as the nearest appropriate focus target outside the repeater, or use a safe recycling path that does not depend on another row accepting focus.

findings.title: The on-screen focus fixture can pass if the reorder immediately steals focus
findings.evidence: FocusedSwappedThenScrolled sets ScrollAwayAfterChange, not ChangeWhileScrolledAway, so it skips the focus assertions after Change. It then scrolls away and back and checks only labels. An implementation that always transfers focus as soon as the reorder completes could prevent stale rows and pass, without exercising the viewport watcher or preserving focus on the correctly displayed row.
findings.recommendation: Assert that the original button still owns focus after the on-screen reorder and before scrolling. Then assert the intended focus handoff after scrolling away, before checking the rows on return.

findings.title: The spec gives conflicting accounts of repeater index lookup
findings.evidence: The existing ItemsRepeater paragraph still says RefreshRealizedItems iterates realized indices and reads Source[i].Key. The new paragraph says the keyed path never asks the repeater by index, while the same section acknowledges that move animation still does. ElementFactory.cs:392–421 changes the lookup specifically for keyed content refresh; the legacy refresh still calls TryGetElement.
findings.recommendation: Replace the obsolete refresh paragraph and scope the index-lookup claim to keyed content reconciliation, explicitly distinguishing legacy refresh and move animation.

findings.title: Replacing the last valid ThemeRef with an invalid key leaves the old brush active
findings.evidence: If a control changes from a valid Foreground ThemeRef to a key containing both quote characters, the new binding is rejected and the zero-setter branch returns without releasing the old Style. Reconciler.Update.cs:164–167 only clears the old Style when ThemeBindings becomes null, so the control keeps following the old resource even though the warning says the property was left unset.
findings.recommendation: When an apply produces no usable setters, call ClearThemeBindings to release only Reactor's owned Style and restore its base. Add a live valid-to-invalid update case.

findings.title: Newly supported resource keys can collide in both Style caches
findings.evidence: BuildCacheKey at lines 643–653 concatenates unescaped property names and resource keys. A Button with only Background bound to the literal key `A|Foreground=B` gets the same cache key as a Button with Background bound to `A` and Foreground bound to `B`. The new formatter accepts the literal key, and both cache paths reuse the first Style before examining the actual bindings.
findings.recommendation: Use a structural cache key or length-prefix each component while keeping the property ordering deterministic. Add a unit test for this pair of binding sets.

findings.title: A second interaction state can overwrite a newer normal brush and restore stale state
findings.evidence: Start hovering a ThemeRef-backed control, then re-render it with an explicit Background while still hovered. ApplyModifiers writes the new brush at lines 7339–7343. If the user presses before leaving, ApplyInteractionBrush overwrites that brush without refreshing normalLocal because overrideApplied is already true. On exit it still owns the active brush and clears the DP using the original snapshot, losing the newly rendered Background.
findings.recommendation: Before each state write, check whether the current local value is still the tracked override. If ownership changed, capture the new normal value before applying the next override. Cover a render between hover and press.

findings.title: A missing SplitView base Style falls through to the write the fix is meant to avoid
findings.evidence: If the application lookup cannot return a Style for DefaultSplitViewStyle, such as when an app resource shadows it with a different type, SplitView is treated as a normal unbased control. ApplyThemeBindings caches the unbased Style before assignment at lines 8429–8440. If a loaded SplitView rejects that assignment as described at lines 8498–8500, a later cache hit retries it outside the catch at lines 8383–8386.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish a missing required base from a control that needs no base. Warn and leave the SplitView untouched if no compatible base can be resolved, and do not cache an unbased Style before successful application.

findings.title: ThemeRef stops applying when an author Style targets a custom control subclass
findings.evidence: A Style targeting an app-defined Button subclass is valid on that subclass. GetExactStyleTargetType at lines 8512–8519 instead chooses the first WinUI ancestor, such as Button. The generated Button Style cannot be BasedOn a Style targeting its subclass, so the new path keeps the author Style but drops ThemeRef; the old unbased Button Style could apply the theme setter. The styling guide's promise that layering works with any Style does not account for this case.
findings.recommendation: Compose against the actual runtime target type when the author base requires it. If that is not supported, preserve the previous theming behavior through an explicit fallback and document the limitation.

findings.title: Pooled controls retain the previous renter's author Style
findings.evidence: The new attached marker holds the author base Style, and the existing ownership marker now also references it through BasedOn. ElementPool.CleanElement at lines 302–308 clears only FrameworkElement.StyleProperty. A pooled TextBlock that used a per-instance Style can therefore retain that Style and its template even after the shared Style cache is cleared.
findings.recommendation: Clear both ownership markers when returning the control to the pool, without restoring the author Style. Keep that reset separate from in-place ThemeRef removal.

findings.title: Invalid-key warnings retain and emit unbounded strings
findings.evidence: The process-wide deduplication dictionary caps entry count, not key length, and the warning interpolates the full rejected key. With diagnostics enabled, an app that passes data-driven keys can retain oversized strings for the lifetime of the process and hand oversized messages to ETW or the debug log. Spec 044 requires bounded payloads; WarnUnresolvedStyle already bounds both retention and emission.
findings.recommendation: Do not retain overlong keys, and truncate and escape control characters in the displayed identifier before logging. Reuse the named-style warning's length policy.

findings.title: No live test proves an invalid key leaves a valid sibling binding intact
findings.evidence: The quoting fixture applies one valid Background key per control. The rejection theories in ReconcilerCacheKeyTests.cs:115–129 only check formatter output. Neither test would fail if the reconciler aborted style synthesis on the first invalid key instead of skipping just that setter.
findings.recommendation: Add a live fixture with an invalid Background key and a valid Foreground key on the same control. Assert that Background falls back and Foreground still responds to a native theme flip.

findings.title: An implicit opacity transition can mask the keyframe XAML stopped
findings.evidence: The check clears its pending state and returns for any non-null opacity controller. But XAML's opacity push can both stop the named keyframe and start an implicit Opacity animation, as documented in spec 066 §3 and exercised by ImplicitAnimationSlotsFixtures.cs:84–91, 129–135. For example, a style-supplied opacity with an `.Animate()` opacity slot can leave the implicit transition running after the first push while the named `fade` never resumes.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish the named keyframe and a transition started by the initial XAML push from an intentional replacement. Add a live fixture with an implicit Opacity slot and assert that the named controller owns the channel after the push.

findings.title: A later style write can resurrect a loop the style was meant to stop
findings.evidence: The check is armed for every opacity keyframe start, including trigger changes on already-rendered controls with no pending base-opacity change. If a style changes Opacity after that trigger update but before the commit callback, XAML stops the loop. The entry still passes `Owns`, and the missing controller causes the loop to restart. This contradicts CHANGELOG.md:158–159, which says a later style change still stops a running keyframe.
findings.recommendation: Arm recovery only for an opacity push already pending when the keyframe starts, and invalidate it when a later effective style value supersedes that push. Test a trigger update followed by a style change before the commit callback.

findings.title: Wall-clock expiry drops finite fades that XAML interrupted
findings.evidence: The stopwatch starts when Reactor submits the animation, before the first render or commit, and the check may run later via the dispatcher. If XAML cancels a finite fade on its first frame but that frame or the callback is delayed past the fade's duration, elapsed wall time makes the cancellation look like natural completion. The fade can be skipped entirely even though it never played for its requested duration.
findings.recommendation: Base recovery on whether the pending XAML push interrupted playback, not on elapsed time since submission. Cover a short fade whose first push preempts it and a separate fade that actually completes.

findings.title: Cancellation leaves the pending layout handler subscribed
findings.evidence: The `LayoutUpdated` delegate is stored only in a local and unsubscribes only when it next fires. Removing the keyframe at line 6923, replacing opacity through AnimationHelper.cs:51, or resetting the control for the pool at line 6983 invalidates ownership but cannot detach the handler. A detached or pooled control can therefore retain the delegate and its captured animation/controller until another layout notification. The existing pool opacity sync explicitly unregisters its handler during unmount for this reason (ElementPool.cs:751–774).
findings.recommendation: Store the pending handler in per-control state and synchronously unsubscribe it on replacement, keyframe removal, unmount, and pool reset, following the pool sync's cancellation pattern.

findings.title: The commit helper silently proceeds on timeout or failure
findings.evidence: `Task.WhenAny` is awaited without checking the winner or awaiting the commit task itself. The fixture samples controllers after `Harness.Render` even when no commit was observed or the commit faulted. `Harness.Render` drains layout and dispatcher work but does not guarantee a XAML render walk, as AnimationCombinationTests.cs:34–40 explains. In particular, the no-restart assertions can pass without observing the commit they are meant to test.
findings.recommendation: Require a successful commit and report timeout or failure explicitly. For assertions about a XAML push, also wait for and verify the relevant render walk.

findings.title: ApplyInteractionBrush clobbers active hover/press brushes on mid-interaction updates and restores stale values across state transitions
findings.evidence: For BorderBrush, ApplyModifiers (lines 7263-7271) checks borderTracker.BorderBrushOverrideApplied so mid-hover updates record the new normal brush on the tracker without overwriting the live hover brush (pinned by PanelBorderFixture phases 8/10/11). The new ApplyInteractionBrush path for Background and Foreground (lines 6246-6264, 6307-6336) leaves ApplyModifiers (lines 7339-7362) and BorderElement.Customize (src/Reactor/Core/Element.cs:4934-4951) uncoordinated and captures normalLocal only when !overrideApplied (lines 6313-6316). When an interactive element re-renders while hovered/pressed/focused (for example, clicking a hovered card or button toggles selection and updates .Background(...) or .Foreground(...)): (1) the reconcile write/ClearValue immediately overwrites the active hover/pressed brush while the pointer is still inside; and (2) because overrideApplied remains true, any subsequent non-Normal transition before exiting to Normal (such as Pressed -> PointerOver on pointer release after click, or PointerOver -> Pressed where MergePressed at line 6196 inherits PointerOver's brush) skips recapturing normalLocal, re-applies stateBrush, and sets activeBrush = stateBrush. When the pointer then exits to Normal, ReferenceEquals(fe.ReadLocalValue(dp), active) (line 6329) is true again and restores the stale pre-click normalLocal: mounting with .Background(Theme.CardBackground) (normalLocal = UnsetValue) and updating on click to .Background(selectedBrush) clears selectedBrush on pointer exit, while mounting with .Background(explicitBrush) and updating on click to .Background(Theme.CardBackground) writes explicitBrush back as a local value and permanently shadows the {ThemeResource} Style setter.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the BorderBrush tracker protocol (lines 7263-7271) in ApplyModifiers for Background (lines 7339-7351) and Foreground (lines 7353-7362) as well as BorderElement.Customize (src/Reactor/Core/Element.cs:4934-4951): when tracker.BackgroundOverrideApplied / ForegroundOverrideApplied is true during reconcile, update tracker.NormalBackground / NormalForeground (to the new Brush on set, or DependencyProperty.UnsetValue on unset) instead of mutating fe's live local property while an interaction override is active, and refresh active state values if ApplyInteractionStates updates Config to drop that state's brush.

findings.title: ApplyThemeBindings leaves the previous themed Style active when an in-place update produces zero valid setters
findings.evidence: Reconciler.Update.cs (lines 166-168) calls ClearThemeBindings(fe) only when oldEl.ThemeBindings is not null && newEl.ThemeBindings is null. If an already-mounted element updates in place from a valid ThemeRef (e.g. .Foreground(Theme.PrimaryText)) to an unrepresentable data-driven ThemeRef (e.g. new ThemeRef("") or new ThemeRef("a'b\"c")), newEl.ThemeBindings is still non-null, so ApplyThemeBindings runs. Every binding is skipped at lines 8401-8405 (where WarnUnrepresentableThemeKey logs that 'the property it binds is left unset'), and line 8410 executes 'if (setters.Length == 0) return;' without calling ClearThemeBindings(fe). As a result, fe.Style keeps the previous render's synthesized {ThemeResource} Style and ReactorAppliedThemeStyleProperty instead of unsetting the binding or restoring ReactorThemeBaseStyleProperty.
findings.recommendation: Call ClearThemeBindings(fe) before returning when setters.Length == 0 at line 8410 (a no-op on initial mount when ReactorAppliedThemeStyleProperty is unset, and restores any author/framework base Style or clears FrameworkElement.StyleProperty on update).

findings.title: Author Styles targeting non-WinUI control subclasses trigger uncached XamlReader.Load and thrown WinRT exceptions on every render
findings.evidence: When a custom or third-party control subclass outside Microsoft.UI.Xaml.* (e.g. an app Control subclass or CommunityToolkit control) carries both an author Style with TargetType = typeof(MyCustomControl) and a ThemeRef modifier, GetExactStyleTargetType (lines 8509-8518) resolves the first Microsoft.UI.Xaml.* base (such as Control or ContentControl). ApplyThemeBindings then parses '<Style TargetType="Control">...</Style>' via XamlReader.Load, sets style.BasedOn = baseStyle, and fails inside TryApplyBasedStyle (lines 8462-8476) with E_INVALIDARG because BasedOn.TargetType is more derived than style.TargetType. Because failed pairs return false before _basedStyleCache.TryAdd (lines 8450-8452), every subsequent re-render of that element misses _basedStyleCache, re-runs XamlReader.Load, throws across WinRT, mutates fe.Style twice, and emits DiagnosticLog.SwallowedError.
findings.recommendation: Have GetExactStyleTargetType return the resolved WinUI System.Type (not just its Name) and check 'baseStyle?.TargetType is { } bt && !bt.IsAssignableFrom(winuiType)' before XamlReader.Load. When incompatible, skip XAML parsing/throwing altogether and emit a deduplicated DiagnosticLog.Warning explaining that ThemeRef cannot layer over a Style targeting a non-WinUI subclass.

findings.title: WarnUnrepresentableThemeKey retains and logs unbounded, unsanitized external keys and goes permanently silent past 256 keys
findings.evidence: Lines 8578-8579 state 'up to a cap that bounds what a data-driven caller could retain', but WarnedThemeKeysCap = 256 bounds only entry count, not per-key string length. Compare ElementExtensions.WarnUnresolvedStyle (src/Reactor/Elements/ElementExtensions.cs:772-816, implementing Spec 044 §6.2.1): (1) a data-driven caller passing oversized bad keys can pin 256 arbitrarily large strings for the process lifetime in static _warnedThemeKeys and interpolate the full un-truncated string—which is guaranteed to have failed FormatThemeResourceReference and may contain raw CR/LF log-splitting characters, XML-illegal control characters, or lone UTF-16 surrogates—into ReactorEventSource.Log.Warning and Debug.WriteLine; and (2) checking '_warnedThemeKeys.Count >= WarnedThemeKeysCap' before emitting suppresses all warnings permanently after 256 distinct bad keys instead of merely skipping deduplication insertion as WarnUnresolvedStyle does.
findings.recommendation: Align WarnUnrepresentableThemeKey with ElementExtensions.WarnUnresolvedStyle and Spec 044 §6.2.1: enforce a MaxKeyChars = 256 cap (never inserting overlong keys into _warnedThemeKeys), truncate and sanitize control characters / lone surrogates in the logged preview before calling DiagnosticLog.Warning, and when _warnedThemeKeys.Count >= WarnedThemeKeysCap for an unseen key, skip _warnedThemeKeys.TryAdd rather than suppressing the warning.

findings.title: Missing selftest coverage for mid-interaction Background/Foreground updates and unrepresentable ThemeRef bindings in ApplyThemeBindings
findings.evidence: Two core runtime paths introduced by this diff are untested: (1) InteractionStatesRestoresCurrentExplicitBrush (lines 201-244) only mutates state (setSecond!(true) at line 231) after SimulatePointerOverForTests(border, isOver: false), leaving updates/clears and Brush-to-ThemeRef or ThemeRef-to-Brush transitions during an active PointerOver/Pressed state completely uncovered (unlike PanelBorderFixture phases 8/10/11 for BorderBrush); and (2) ReconcilerCacheKeyTests (tests/Reactor.Tests/ReconcilerCacheKeyTests.cs:113-133) tests only pure FormatThemeResourceReference, with no test in ThemeRefStyleFixtures or Reactor.Tests exercising ApplyThemeBindings when a key is unrepresentable (verifying that valid sibling ThemeRef setters on the same element still apply, that updating from a valid key to an invalid key clears the old themed Style, and that WarnUnrepresentableThemeKey emits/deduplicates its ETW warning as NamedStyleResolutionFixture does for WarnUnresolvedStyle).

On a control whose composition visual has already been acquired, ApplyTransitions writes the opacity fallback into Visual.ImplicitAnimations. findings.title: Removing a transition declines the skip but leaves the transition installed

findings.title: MoveFocusOffStaleContainer leaves focus on the stale or deleted container when no other realized row accepts focus
findings.evidence: RefreshRealizedItems (src/Reactor/Core/ElementFactory.cs:375-379) clears _listState.PinnedIndicesMayBeStale = false before scheduling RunFocusedContainerCheck. MoveFocusOffStaleContainer (src/Reactor/Core/ElementFactory.StaleContainers.cs:108-131) gathers realized controls from _keyByControl excluding stale and loops `if (control.Focus(state)) return;`. When `candidates` is empty (e.g., deleting the sole item or clearing the list via KeyedListDiff fast path 4) or every candidate returns false (e.g., a focused interactive row scrolled off screen is moved/removed while all currently realized rows are read-only non-focusable elements, which lines 106-107 note refuse focus), the method returns with focus still on `stale`. Because PinnedIndicesMayBeStale was already cleared, `stale` remains pinned with keyboard focus on a stale/deleted subtree, and scrolling back to `staleIndex` — or repopulating an emptied list via Source.Add (KeyedListDiff.cs:339-353), which does not set PinnedIndicesMayBeStale (src/Reactor/Core/Internal/ReactorListState.cs:153-155) — lets ItemsRepeater hand `stale` back for its old index without calling GetElement.
findings.recommendation: Add a fallback after the `candidates` loop when focus remains inside `stale`: move focus to a focusable element outside `repeater` within `repeater.XamlRoot` (for example via FocusManager.FindNextElement / FocusManager.FindFirstFocusableElement excluding descendants of `stale`), and if nothing else in the window can take focus, transiently collapse and restore `stale` (using GetParkingContent for ItemContainer and preserving local VisibilityProperty) so XAML releases focus and ItemsRepeater drops the pin.

findings.title: Post-layout focus check does not force re-realization when ItemsRepeater already handed the stale pinned container back during that layout pass
findings.evidence: ScheduleFocusedContainerCheck (src/Reactor/Core/ElementFactory.StaleContainers.cs:32-38) defers RunFocusedContainerCheck to `repeater.LayoutUpdated`, which fires after measure and arrange complete for the collection change. If the same update that left a focused off-screen container at a stale index in the pinned pool also brings `staleIndex` into the realization window during that layout pass (for example, deleting several rows while scrolled down reduces ScrollableHeight so the viewport clamps onto `staleIndex`), ItemsRepeater hands `stale` from the pinned pool back to layout for `staleIndex` during measure before line 99 moves focus off it. Once layout actively owns `stale` at `staleIndex`, unpinning it via focus transfer does not recycle an on-screen realized container, leaving `stale` rendered at `staleIndex` with no `_controlByKey` entry for `listState.Source[staleIndex].Key`.
findings.recommendation: After moving focus off `child` in RunFocusedContainerCheck, if `index >= 0 && index < listState.Source.Count` (when `child` is already serving `index` in layout), call `ScheduleReRealize(listState.Source[index].Key)` so FlushReRealize (src/Reactor/Core/ElementFactory.cs:587-619) emits a Replace notification on `listState.Source[index]` now that `child` is unpinned, forcing ItemsRepeater to recycle `child` and realize the true row through GetElement.

findings.title: Unmounted selection markers fail to invalidate idle scopes because Unloaded walks a detached parent chain
findings.evidence: Idle scopes now detach from LayoutUpdated in MarkdownSelectionHost.UpdateLayoutTracking (MarkdownSelectionHost.cs:111-119) and rely on MarkdownSelectionMarker.InvalidateEnclosingScope() to schedule a refresh. MarkdownSelectionMarker wires `Unloaded += (_, _) => InvalidateEnclosingScope()` (line 146), where InvalidateEnclosingScope() walks `VisualTreeHelper.GetParent(parent)` from `this` (lines 149-154), and MarkdownSelectionHandler.Unmount (lines 207-212) clears `marker.Child = null` without calling `marker.InvalidateEnclosingScope()`. In WinUI 3, `Unloaded` fires asynchronously after the unmounted element or its ancestor has already been removed from its parent in the live visual tree (and as ElementPool.cs:195 notes, `VisualTreeHelper.GetParent` requires a live visual tree). When a conditional child surface unmounts inside a stretched layout or as the only surface in an idle scope (where no surviving sibling MarkdownSelectionMarker fires SizeChanged), `InvalidateEnclosingScope()` terminates at null without reaching `MarkdownSelectionHost`, leaving the unmounted marker and stale text in `_surfaces` and `Document.Text`.
findings.recommendation: Cache the enclosing `MarkdownSelectionHost` (for example in a `WeakReference<MarkdownSelectionHost>`) on `MarkdownSelectionMarker` when `Loaded` or `InvalidateEnclosingScope()` resolves it so `Unloaded` can invalidate that scope after detachment, and call `marker.InvalidateEnclosingScope()` in `MarkdownSelectionHandler.Unmount` while the marker is still parented.

findings.title: Click-away stops clearing the collapsed caret after the double-click timeout and leaves the caret suppressed during keyboard navigation
findings.evidence: UpdateClickAwayRegistration() activates `MarkdownSelectionClickAway` only when `Document.Start != Document.End || _clicks.IsPending` (line 153), while DrawSelection() paints a visible caret whenever `Document.Start == Document.End && !_suppressCaret && FocusState != FocusState.Unfocused && Document.Text.Length > 0` (lines 1176-1181). After a single click places a collapsed caret, `_clickTimer` fires after `GetDoubleClickTime()` (~500ms) and `ResetClickSequence()` unregisters the host from `MarkdownSelectionClickAway` while the caret remains visible. A subsequent primary click on non-focusable outside chrome (such as `SelectionBlank`) does not move WinUI focus and never invokes `ClearForClickAway()`, leaving the caret stuck on screen and contradicting `docs/_pipeline/templates/text-and-media.md.dt` lines 269-270 ('clears its highlight and collapsed text range'). The same gap occurs after collapsing a selection with Escape/arrows or focusing via Tab (`OnFocusChanged` lines 101-110 never calls `UpdateClickAwayRegistration()`). Conversely, when `ClearForClickAway()` (lines 743-750) sets `_suppressCaret = true` on a click to non-focusable space (`FocusState` stays `Pointer`), pressing arrow/Home/End keys in `HandleKey` (lines 752-787) moves `Document.Caret` without firing `GotFocus`, so `_suppressCaret` remains `true` and hides the caret (and `ClearForClickAway()` calls `ResetClickSequence()` before setting `_suppressCaret = true`).
findings.recommendation: Define a shared `HasVisibleCaret` helper (`Document.Start == Document.End && !_suppressCaret && FocusState != FocusState.Unfocused && Document.Text.Length > 0`), include `HasVisibleCaret` in `UpdateClickAwayRegistration()`, call `UpdateClickAwayRegistration()` in `OnFocusChanged` and after setting `_suppressCaret = true` in `ClearForClickAway()`, and clear `_suppressCaret = false` on caret-moving keys in `HandleKey`.

findings.title: UpdateLayoutTracking detaches while a collapsed caret is visible, losing the caret after async scroll-into-view or viewport scrolling
findings.evidence: `OnFocusChanged` calls `UpdateLayoutTracking()` (line 109), yet `UpdateLayoutTracking()` computes `track = !_detached && _loaded && (_refreshPending || _pointer is not null || _nativePressOwner is not null || Document.Start != Document.End)` (lines 113-114), omitting the visible collapsed-caret state drawn by `DrawSelection()` (lines 1176-1181). When `Document.Start == Document.End` with a visible caret and the user presses `Down`, `PageDown`, or `End` without Shift to reach a clipped surface inside `ItemsView`/`ScrollView`, `HandleKey` (lines 774-785) calls `DrawSelection()` synchronously before `StartBringIntoView` asynchronously scrolls `ScrollView` via `InteractionTracker` (see `MarkdownSelectionFixtures.cs:607`), so `Intersect(CharacterBounds(Document.Caret), viewport)` clips the caret to zero height. When `ScrollView` finishes scrolling on subsequent frames, `LayoutUpdated` is detached so `OnLayout` never runs to redraw the caret; likewise, wheel-scrolling an outer `ScrollViewer`/`ScrollView` never updates viewport clipping of a visible collapsed caret.
findings.recommendation: Include the visible-caret condition (`!_suppressCaret && FocusState != FocusState.Unfocused && Document.Text.Length > 0`) in `UpdateLayoutTracking()` so `LayoutUpdated` remains attached while either a selection range or a collapsed caret is rendered in `_overlay`.

findings.title: ITextRangeProvider.Move(TextUnit.Paragraph) expands degenerate insertion points instead of keeping them collapsed
findings.evidence: `MarkdownSelectionRangeMovement.Move` (`MarkdownTextSelection.cs:278-285`) implements the UIA `ITextRangeProvider.Move` contract verified by `UiaMove_PreservesInsertionPointsAndFailedNonEmptyRanges` (`MarkdownTextSelectionTests.cs:498`) and `MdSelection_UiaMoveKeepsInsertionPoint` (`MarkdownSelectionFixtures.cs:465`): moving a degenerate range (`_start == _end`) moves the insertion point without expanding it (`result.Start == result.End`), whereas moving a non-empty range expands to the target unit. In `MarkdownSelectionRange.Move` (lines 174-178), the new `if (unit == TextUnit.Paragraph && result.Moved != 0 && result.Start < host.Document.Text.Length)` branch unconditionally replaces `result` with `host.Document.UnitAt(MarkdownSelectionUnit.Paragraph, result.Start)` even when `_start == _end`. Calling `peer.Range(0, 0).Move(TextUnit.Paragraph, 1)` therefore expands a collapsed insertion point to the entire second paragraph (`(17, 32)`), while `Move(TextUnit.Paragraph, 2)` at `Text.Length` stays collapsed (`(32, 32)`), and `MdSelection_UiaParagraphMoveForwardAcrossSurfaces` (`MarkdownSelectionFixtures.cs:406-412`) encodes this inverted behavior on `peer.Range(0, 0)`.
findings.recommendation: Capture `bool isDegenerate = _start == _end;` before moving and apply the `UnitAt(MarkdownSelectionUnit.Paragraph, result.Start)` span trim only when `!isDegenerate` (updating `MdSelection_UiaParagraphMoveForwardAcrossSurfaces` to call `paragraph.ExpandToEnclosingUnit(TextUnit.Paragraph)` on the initial range before calling `Move`).

findings.title: EmbeddedControls maps custom LinkBuilder controls with non-verbatim text to zero-width UIA ranges
findings.evidence: `SurfaceTextSegments` (lines 1126-1132) supports `IsLink` surfaces whose native `TextSegments` do not concatenate to `marker.Metadata.Text` (such as image links `[![alt](img)](https://...)`, icon-prefixed link buttons, or custom `Surface` labels) by returning `[new TextSegment(marker, marker.Metadata.Text, null, marker)]` with `Owner = marker` (the inner `MarkdownSelectionMarker`). However, `EmbeddedControls()` skips `MarkdownSelectionMarker` (line 1256) and matches each embedded `Control` `child` using `if (IsDescendantOf(segment.Owner, child))` (line 1272). Because `segment.Owner` (`marker`) is an ancestor of `child` rather than a descendant of `child`, `IsDescendantOf(marker, child)` returns `false`, `start` remains `-1`, and lines 1279-1284 collapse the control's range to `(start, start)`. Consequently, `ITextProvider.RangeFromChild` returns an empty insertion-point range instead of `link.Text`, and `ITextRangeProvider.GetChildren()` omits the control on subranges of `link.Text` past its start offset.
findings.recommendation: Treat segments owned by an enclosing `IsLink` marker as belonging to the embedded control in `EmbeddedControls()`, e.g. `if (IsDescendantOf(segment.Owner, child) || (segment.Owner is MarkdownSelectionMarker { Metadata.IsLink: true } linkMarker && IsDescendantOf(child, linkMarker)))`.

findings.title: Cross-surface Shift+drag corrupts selection anchor when streaming rebuilds the document
findings.evidence: In `OnPressed` (lines 558-563), Shift+click keeps `_dragUnit == MarkdownSelectionUnit.Character`, computes `anchor = PointerAnchor(Document.Anchor, offset, e.KeyModifiers)` (which retains `Document.Anchor` from whichever surface originally held the anchor), and sets `_pressSpan = new(anchor, anchor)`. Lines 562-563 then compute `_pressLocalSpan = new(_pressSpan.Start - entry.Start, _pressSpan.End - entry.Start)` and `_pressSurfaceIdentity = entry.Identity` relative to the clicked `entry` rather than `Document.EntryAt(anchor)`. If `Document.Anchor` is in an earlier surface (`_pressLocalSpan.Start < 0`) or a later surface (`_pressLocalSpan.Start > entry.Text.Length`) and a streaming update rebuilds the document mid-drag (`Refresh`, lines 335-339), `Math.Clamp(_pressLocalSpan.Start, 0, pressedEntry.Text.Length)` snaps `_pressSpan` onto `pressedEntry`'s start or end, jumping the anchor into the clicked surface. Similarly, a triple-click drag (`_dragUnit == MarkdownSelectionUnit.Paragraph`) clamps `_pressLocalSpan.End` to the pre-stream length instead of `pressedEntry.End`, dropping newly streamed tail text from the pressed paragraph.
findings.recommendation: Record `_pressSurfaceIdentity` and `_pressLocalSpan` against `var anchorEntry = _dragUnit == MarkdownSelectionUnit.Character ? Document.EntryAt(anchor) ?? entry : entry;`, and when `_dragUnit == MarkdownSelectionUnit.Paragraph` update `_pressSpan` to `new(pressedEntry.Start, pressedEntry.End)` on document rebuild.

findings.title: MarkdownSelectionClickAway.Router caches initial XamlRoot.Content and stops routing clicks when root content changes
findings.evidence: `MarkdownSelectionClickAway.Router` captures `_content = root.Content` once in its constructor (line 1324) and attaches/detaches `UIElement.PointerPressedEvent` only on that cached instance (lines 1335, 1341). `XamlRoot.Content` is not immutable for the lifetime of a `XamlRoot`: `ReactorHost` replaces `_window.Content` when wrapping/unwrapping the dev overlay (`ReactorHost.cs:1338-1385`) without unloading existing controls, and root content swaps can activate a new `MarkdownSelectionHost` before the prior tree's asynchronous WinUI `Unloaded` removes the `Router` entry from `Routers`. Once `root.Content` moves off the cached `_content`, `_pressed` stays attached to a detached `UIElement` and click-away stops firing (and if `Router.OnPressed` lines 1358-1363 prunes dead `WeakReference` entries down to `_hosts.Count == 0`, `_pressed` is not detached from `_content`).
findings.recommendation: Store `XamlRoot` in `Router`, rebind `_pressed` onto ` _root.Content` whenever `!ReferenceEquals(_content, _root.Content)` during `SetActive`, and remove the handler / router entry if dead-reference pruning in `OnPressed` leaves `_hosts` empty.

findings.title: Click-away E2E assertions race asynchronous SendInput delivery, and custom LinkBuilder fallback segments have no test coverage
findings.evidence: In `Selection_RoutedInputAndExternalEvents` (lines 284-294), `Click(currentInnerX, currentInnerY)` injects `SendInput` down/up without waiting for cross-process delivery, and lines 286 and 292 immediately call `Wait(() => innerText.GetSelection().Single().GetText(-1) == "")` when the selection text is already `""` from line 279. Because the predicate is already true before the host window processes the click, `Wait` can succeed on its first poll even if the click would select a word once delivered (unlike line 141, which synchronizes on `HelpText`'s `pressCount` first), and no test exercises click-away after `GetDoubleClickTime()` expires. Additionally, every `LinkBuilder` selection test (`MarkdownTextSelectionTests.cs:92`, `MarkdownSelectionFixtures.cs:397`, `MarkdownSelectionInputFixture.cs:42`) uses `link => Button(link.Text)`, leaving the new synthetic `SurfaceTextSegments` / `ComputeCharacterBounds` fallback (`MarkdownSelectionHost.cs:1009, 1126-1132`) unexercised across all test tiers.
findings.recommendation: Synchronize lines 286 and 292 on `inner.Current.HelpText` advancing `pressCount` before asserting `GetSelection().Single().GetText(-1) == ""`, add a click-away check after the double-click timeout expires (verifying the caret overlay is cleared), and add a selftest for a `LinkBuilder` whose rendered visual text differs from `link.Text` (such as an image or icon-prefixed link button) covering hit-testing, selection, and `RangeFromChild`.

findings.title: Elapsed-time guard in RestartOpacityAfterXamlPush suppresses restart of finite keyframes after delayed/collapsed first render or short durations
findings.evidence: In `src/Reactor/Core/Reconciler.cs:6754` and `6800-6803`, `startedAt` is stamped when `RestartOpacityAfterXamlPush` is called during `Mount`/`Update`, and `Check()` aborts when `Stopwatch.GetElapsedTime(startedAt) >= finite.Duration * finite.IterationCount` under the comment `// A finite keyframe that simply finished is not restarted.` However, in WinUI Composition an undisturbed finite `KeyFrameAnimation` that finishes retains its `AnimationController` on the visual (`docs/specs/066-transforms-on-composition-visual.md:935`: "A finished animation also keeps its controller, so `TryGetAnimationController` is not a 'still running' test"; `tests/Reactor.AppTests.Host/SelfTest/Fixtures/TransformsMatrixRecorder.cs:666`; `transforms-ledger.json:451` where a 30 ms one-shot opacity keyframe still reports `"running": "Opacity"` after `Settle()`). Consequently, when XAML did not push `Opacity`, line `6799` (`if (visual.TryGetAnimationController("Opacity") is not null) return;`) already prevents replaying a finished keyframe; reaching line `6801` means XAML's first-render opacity push cleared the controller and overwrote `visual.Opacity` with `UIElement.Opacity` before a single visible frame showed the animation. Concrete failures: (1) Mounting `Border(...).Opacity(0.4).Keyframes("fade", 1, kf => kf.Duration(300).At(0, opacity: 0f).At(1, opacity: 1f))` inside a `Visibility.Collapsed` ancestor (promised in `docs/specs/066-transforms-on-composition-visual.md:141-144`) and revealing it after 300 ms causes XAML's first-render push to clobber `visual.Opacity` to `0.4` while line `6803` aborts the restart (`TransformModifierFixtures.cs:480-484` missed this because `"Collapsed"` used infinite-loop `OpacityPulse` and `"Finite"` used 60,000 ms `LongFade`). (2) In `TransformModifierFixtures.cs:518-530` (`TransformKeyframes_FinishedOpacityKeyframeNotReplayed`), `plain.Opacity(0.4).Keyframes("fade", 1, kf => kf.Duration(1).At(0, opacity: 1).At(1, opacity: 0.5f))` saw `TryGetAnimationController("Opacity") is null` only because XAML's push clobbered the 1 ms keyframe back to `0.4f` instead of `0.5f`; any short finite keyframe (e.g. `Duration(30)` in `TransformsMatrixRecorder.cs:218`) similarly fails to restart whenever initial layout, commit, and `DispatcherQueue` dispatch exceed `Duration` under load.
findings.recommendation: Remove `startedAt` (`line 6754`) and the `Stopwatch.GetElapsedTime(startedAt) >= finite.Duration * finite.IterationCount` guard (`lines 6800-6803`), relying on line `6799` to leave undisturbed finished finite keyframes untouched while restarting whenever XAML's first-render push cleared the controller. Update `TransformKeyframes_FinishedOpacityKeyframeNotReplayed` in `TransformModifierFixtures.cs:516-532` to omit `.Opacity(0.4)` (verifying an undisturbed `Duration(1)` keyframe is not restarted and settles at `0.5f`), and add a collapsed-ancestor test case using a finite keyframe whose `Duration` elapses while collapsed before flipping to `Visibility.Visible`.

findings.title: Deferred render wait in RestartOpacityAfterXamlPush misses Popup/Flyout trees and leaves LayoutUpdated subscribed if unmounted before render
findings.evidence: When `!IsRendered(fe)` holds after the initial commit, `Check()` (`src/Reactor/Core/Reconciler.cs:6784-6797`) subscribes only `fe.LayoutUpdated += onLayout` (citing `ElementPool`'s renter sync at line `6787`), where `IsRendered(fe)` (`lines 6818-6824`) checks `fe.IsLoaded || ElementPool.IsInLiveTree(fe)`. Unlike `ElementPool.SyncOpacityWhenLoaded` (`src/Reactor/Core/ElementPool.cs:733-783`), this omits both `fe.Loaded` and unmount cleanup: (1) `ElementPool.IsInLiveTree(fe)` walks `VisualTreeHelper.GetParent` to `fe.XamlRoot?.Content`, which is always `false` inside a `Popup`, `Flyout`, or `ContentDialog` rooted under WinUI's `PopupRoot` (`ElementPool.cs:735`). `OverlayLifecycle.MountFlyout` (`src/Reactor/Core/V1Protocol/OverlayLifecycle.cs:521`) and `MountPopup` (`line 757`) eagerly mount content while closed (`IsOpen == false`). When the popup/flyout opens, WinUI runs its opening layout pass before raising `Loaded`: `onLayout` sees `!fe.IsLoaded && !IsInLiveTree(fe)` and returns early, and when `Loaded` fires after layout settles, nothing schedules `RequestCheck()` unless another layout pass later occurs, leaving XAML's first-frame opacity push un-restarted. (2) Unlike `ElementPool.CancelOpacitySync` (`ElementPool.cs:757`, called from `Reconciler.CleanupElementChainForUnmount` at `Reconciler.cs:4762` so unattached controls do not stay on WinUI's window-wide `LayoutUpdated` list), `RestartOpacityAfterXamlPush` keeps `onLayout` only in a local closure and never unsubscribes on unmount or `DetachReactorState` (`Reconciler.cs:2420`, which also does not clear `state.KeyframeOpacityCheck`), keeping unrendered unmounted controls and captured `Visual`/`AnimationController` references on the layout list until a subsequent layout pass runs.
findings.recommendation: Follow the same pattern as `ElementPool.SyncOpacityWhenLoaded` and `CancelOpacitySync`: subscribe to `fe.Loaded` alongside `fe.LayoutUpdated` so popup/flyout subtrees schedule `RequestCheck()` once `Loaded` fires after initial layout, store the pending handler reference on `ReactorState`, and unsubscribe it (plus clear `state.KeyframeOpacityCheck = null`) when cancelled, unmounted (`CleanupElementChainForUnmount` / `ForgetCompositionState`), or detached (`DetachReactorState`).

findings.title: Click-away misses clicks inside popup-hosted conversations
findings.evidence: The router listens only on XamlRoot.Content. Reactor's OverlayLifecycle.cs:301–302 establishes that ContentDialog content lives in a separate popup root. If a dialog contains a Markdown message and a sibling composer, clicking the composer does not route through the subscribed content element. Losing focus redraws the nonempty selection rather than clearing it.
findings.recommendation: Observe presses on the popup routing tree as well as the main content tree. Add an input test that selects text in a ContentDialog and clicks its composer, asserting both selection dismissal and composer focus.

findings.title: Click-away stops observing a visible caret when the click timer expires
findings.evidence: A single click focuses the host and draws a collapsed caret. Once the multiclick timer expires, ResetClickSequence unregisters the host because the range is empty. DrawSelection still shows the caret while the host is focused, so a later click on non-focusable chat background never calls ClearForClickAway and leaves the caret visible.
findings.recommendation: Keep the host registered while it has a visible caret, update registration on focus changes, and test a background click after the multiclick interval has expired.

findings.title: A document update can move a Shift-drag anchor to the wrong surface
findings.evidence: OnPressed saves the existing Shift anchor relative to the surface under the pointer (lines 559–563), even if the anchor belongs to another paragraph. When a streamed update rebuilds the document during the drag, Refresh clamps that relative offset to the pressed surface. For example, an anchor in paragraph one and a Shift press in paragraph two produce a negative local offset; the next drag update starts at paragraph two instead, even though Document.Rebuild already remapped the original anchor.
findings.recommendation: For character drags, use the remapped Document.Anchor after rebuilding. Keep surface-relative remapping for word and paragraph gestures, and test a cross-surface Shift-drag while another paragraph changes.

findings.title: Hit testing scans glyphs in preceding offscreen paragraphs
findings.evidence: The old hit test visited surfaces in lower-bound distance order and stopped once no remaining surface could win. The new loop visits document order. With a drag point near the bottom of a long message, each successive paragraph above the point is closer than the last, so the pruning condition admits each paragraph's glyph loop before reaching the actual hit. On a cold cache this performs native geometry queries for offscreen text on the pointer path.
findings.recommendation: Visit the nearest plausible surface first, then prune the rest by their bounds. Add a long-message regression check that counts character geometry lookups for a hit near the end.

findings.title: The custom-link drag test can bypass the native capture handoff
findings.evidence: The test begins its drag at the same coordinates immediately after a successful link click. Within the system double-click interval, that press selects a word and takes capture in OnPressed, bypassing the first-press path that leaves capture with the button until movement. The test then checks only for nonempty selection inside the label, so the word selected on press can satisfy it without proving the drag changed the range.
findings.recommendation: Reset the click sequence between the activation and drag cases. Assert that the first press leaves a collapsed range, then verify that moving while held extends that range without incrementing the button's click count.

findings.title: The triple-click assertion makes the Ctrl+A event check non-discriminating
findings.evidence: Before Ctrl+A is sent, triple-click has already selected the entire inner document. The following checks look for that same text in the selection and in the shared event queue. Both checks can pass with Ctrl+A disabled because the triple-click produced the required state and event.
findings.recommendation: Start the Ctrl+A check from a verified collapsed or partial range, record an event baseline, and require a new full-document selection event after the keystroke.

findings.title: RestartOpacityAfterXamlPush overwrites ScrollLinked expressions and Spring animations on Opacity
findings.evidence: `RestartOpacityAfterXamlPush` only clears `state.KeyframeOpacityCheck` on `.Opacity(...)` modifier writes/resets (`AnimationHelper.cs:51,208`) and unmount (`Reconciler.cs:6983`), and `Check()` relies on `visual.TryGetAnimationController("Opacity") is not null` (`Reconciler.cs:6799`) to detect whether an animation still occupies the channel. In `Microsoft.UI.Composition`, `Visual.TryGetAnimationController` returns a controller only for `KeyFrameAnimation`s; it returns `null` when an `ExpressionAnimation` or `SpringScalarNaturalMotionAnimation` is playing. `Reconciler.Mount` (`Reconciler.Mount.cs:282-286`) and `Reconciler.Update` (`Reconciler.Update.cs:528-537`) both call `ApplyScrollAnimation` (`Reconciler.cs:6996-7011`) immediately after `ApplyKeyframeAnimations`: when `.ScrollLinked` binds `"Opacity"` (`FadeIn`, `FadeOut`, or `Expression("Opacity", ...)` in `ScrollAnimation.cs:37,47`), `visual.StartAnimation("Opacity", animation)` stops the keyframe controller and leaves `TryGetAnimationController("Opacity") == null` without clearing `KeyframeOpacityCheck`. On the next commit, even with no `UIElement.Opacity` change, `Check()` sees `Owns(...) == true` and `TryGetAnimationController("Opacity") is null` and restarts the keyframe, clobbering the scroll-linked expression. The same false-positive restart overwrites `SpringCurve` (`AnimationHelper.CreateScalarTargetAnimation`, `AnimationHelper.cs:346-356`) fades started before `Check()` runs by `TransitionToState` (`Reconciler.cs:6369`), `ApplyExitTransition` (`Reconciler.cs:6147`), or `TryApplyAmbientExit` (`Reconciler.cs:5194` with `AnimationKind.Spring` at `AnimationKindMap.cs:31`).
findings.recommendation: Clear `state.KeyframeOpacityCheck` (or call a shared helper that cancels the pending opacity keyframe check) in every Reactor path that intentionally writes or starts an animation on `visual`'s `"Opacity"` channel—including `ApplyScrollAnimation` when `expr.Property == "Opacity"`, `TransitionToState`, `ApplyExitTransition`, `TryApplyAmbientExit`, and `TransitionEngine` fade helpers—instead of inferring channel ownership solely from `TryGetAnimationController("Opacity") is not null`.

findings.title: Check() fails to restart the keyframe when XAML's opacity push fires an implicit Opacity animation
findings.evidence: At `Reconciler.cs:6799`, `Check()` bails out whenever `visual.TryGetAnimationController("Opacity") is not null` rather than checking whether the running controller is still `controller`. As documented in `docs/specs/066-transforms-on-composition-visual.md:137` (Q4c) and `PoolLaneFixtures.cs:529`, XAML pushing `UIElement.Opacity` to `visual.Opacity` fires `visual.ImplicitAnimations["Opacity"]` (for example on a visual-lane control re-entering a tree with an implicit `Style` `Opacity` setter, or when `UIElement.Opacity` changes via `.Set(...)` or `WithoutAnimation` alongside a keyframe trigger update while `.Animate()` or a visual-published `.OpacityTransition()` claims `"Opacity"`). As verified by `TransformsMatrixFixture.cs:377-387` (`ImplicitController`), an implicit `ScalarKeyFrameAnimation` exposes its own `AnimationController` via `TryGetAnimationController("Opacity")`. Consequently, `TryGetAnimationController("Opacity")` returns the implicit transition's controller (non-null, `!= controller`), so `Check()` returns early without restarting the keyframe and leaves `started["Opacity"]` and `KeyframeChannelOwners[AnimateProperty.Opacity].DeferredController` pointing at the stopped `controller`.
findings.recommendation: Once intentional Reactor writes/animations on `"Opacity"` clear `state.KeyframeOpacityCheck`, change `Reconciler.cs:6799` from `if (visual.TryGetAnimationController("Opacity") is not null) return;` to `if (Equals(visual.TryGetAnimationController("Opacity"), controller)) return;` so `Check()` restarts the keyframe whenever XAML's push displaced `controller`, even if an implicit `"Opacity"` animation started in its place.

findings.title: Unrendered wait path leaks LayoutUpdated handlers on unmount/replacement and misses popup Loaded
findings.evidence: When `!IsRendered(fe)` holds (`Reconciler.cs:6784-6797`), `RestartOpacityAfterXamlPush` attaches `fe.LayoutUpdated += onLayout` with no cancellation hook on `ReactorState` and no `fe.Loaded` subscription, diverging from `ElementPool.SyncOpacityWhenLoaded` (`ElementPool.cs:732-784`) that line 6787 cites. This creates two defects: (1) In WinUI, `FrameworkElement.LayoutUpdated` subscribes to the thread-wide layout event list. If an off-tree or collapsed control is unmounted/pooled before a layout pass runs (cf. `PoolLaneFixtures.cs:562-569`, `_CancelledBeforeAttach_Released`) or its keyframe trigger updates repeatedly while unrendered, `ForgetCompositionState` / `MarkCompositionWrite` / `RestartOpacityAfterXamlPush` never unsubscribes `onLayout`, keeping `fe`, `visual`, `animation`, `controller`, and `state` rooted on the window layout list (and walking `VisualTreeHelper.GetParent` on every unrelated window layout pass while collapsed). (2) Inside a `Popup` or `Flyout`, `ElementPool.IsInLiveTree(fe)` (`ElementPool.cs:777-783`) is always `false` because the popup subtree terminates at `PopupRoot` rather than `fe.XamlRoot.Content`, and as `ElementPool.cs:734-736` notes, WinUI can raise `Loaded` after the initial layout pass. When popup layout runs while `fe.IsLoaded` is still `false` and `Loaded` subsequently fires and renders without another layout pass, nothing re-invokes `RequestCheck()` once `IsRendered(fe)` becomes `true`.
findings.recommendation: Follow the same lifecycle pattern as `ElementPool.SyncOpacityWhenLoaded` / `CancelOpacitySync` (`ElementPool.cs:737-775`): store the pending `LayoutUpdated`/`Loaded` handler on `ReactorState`, subscribe to `fe.Loaded` alongside `fe.LayoutUpdated` so popup/flyout content re-checks when `Loaded` fires after layout, and unsubscribe immediately whenever `KeyframeOpacityCheck` is replaced or cleared (including `ForgetCompositionState`, `MarkCompositionWrite`, `ClearCompositionOwnership`, and `ElementPool.Return`).

findings.title: DeferredOpacityResetFollowsRestart does not verify a restart occurred and misses non-modifier Opacity interactions
findings.evidence: In `TransformKeyframes_DeferredOpacityResetFollowsRestart` (`TransformModifierFixtures.cs:556-585`), `loopRestarted` (`lines 572-573`) only checks `Equals(running, Reconciler.KeyframeControllerForTests(control, "fade", "Opacity"))` without recording the pre-render controller or checking `Reconciler.KeyframeOpacityRestartsForTests` (unlike the preceding fixtures at `lines 493-511, 523-529, 542-549`, and unlike `lines 494-499` it does not wait for an off-tree commit before `H.SetContent(control)`). If no restart happened (`restarts == 0`), `running`, `KeyframeControllerForTests`, and `owner.DeferredController` all remain the initial controller, and `reconciler.Update(loop, scaleOnly, ...)` calls `ResetCompositionModifier` which writes `(float)element.Opacity` (`0.65f`, `AnimationHelper.cs:189`), so every assertion at `lines 581-583` passes vacuously without exercising `Reconciler.cs:6807-6809`. The fixture suite also lacks selftests for `.Keyframes` combined with `.ScrollLinked` opacity, XAML style pushes when `ImplicitAnimations["Opacity"]` is active on a recycled/live control, and unmounting an off-tree control while `RestartOpacityAfterXamlPush`'s layout wait is pending.
findings.recommendation: Capture `restartsBefore = Reconciler.KeyframeOpacityRestartsForTests` (and/or the initial `AnimationController` before `H.SetContent(control)`) in `TransformKeyframes_DeferredOpacityResetFollowsRestart` and assert `restarts == 1` and `!Equals(running, initialController)`. findings.title: SurfaceTextSegments fallback breaks UIA GetChildren and RangeFromChild when LinkBuilder text differs from link.Text
findings.evidence: When marker.Metadata.IsLink is true and the rendered descendant text runs do not equal marker.Metadata.Text (for example, LinkBuilder = link => Button($"{link.Text} ↗") or an icon/badge button), SurfaceTextSegments (lines 1126-1132) returns [new TextSegment(marker, marker.Metadata.Text, null, marker)] with Owner set to the outer link MarkdownSelectionMarker. However, EmbeddedControls() (lines 1268-1282) associates segments with each descendant Control via IsDescendantOf(segment.Owner, child) (line 1270). Because the link MarkdownSelectionMarker is the parent/ancestor of the Button rather than a descendant of it, IsDescendantOf(marker, child) evaluates to false and EmbeddedControls() falls back to a zero-length insertion point (start == end) at the control's top-left corner (lines 1276-1281). Consequently, MarkdownSelectionAutomationPeer.RangeFromChild(button) returns an empty collapsed range instead of link.Text, and MarkdownSelectionRange.GetChildren() (MarkdownSelectionAutomationPeer.cs:143-145, which checks c.Start < _end && c.End > _start) returns [] for FindText(link.Text) — and even for DocumentRange.GetChildren() itself when the link starts at offset 0 (0 < _end && 0 > 0 is false).
findings.recommendation: Set Owner on the fallback TextSegment in SurfaceTextSegments to (marker.Child as FrameworkElement) ?? marker, or update EmbeddedControls() (line 1270) to also match segments whose Owner is an enclosing MarkdownSelectionMarker { Metadata.IsLink: true } ancestor of child.

findings.title: MarkdownSelectionRange.Move(TextUnit.Paragraph, count) expands degenerate insertion points into full-paragraph selections
findings.evidence: MarkdownSelectionRangeMovement.Move (MarkdownTextSelection.cs:268-274) keeps degenerate ranges (start == end) collapsed at (boundaries[target], boundaries[target], moved), matching UIA's ITextRangeProvider.Move specification and the repository's MdSelection_UiaMoveKeepsInsertionPoint check (MarkdownSelectionFixtures.cs:473-478). However, MarkdownSelectionRange.Move (lines 174-178) overwrites (_start, _end) with host.Document.UnitAt(MarkdownSelectionUnit.Paragraph, result.Start) whenever unit == TextUnit.Paragraph && result.Moved != 0 && result.Start < host.Document.Text.Length, without checking whether the range was non-empty. Calling peer.Range(0, 0).Move(TextUnit.Paragraph, 1) on a multi-paragraph document therefore expands a collapsed insertion point into a full selection of the second paragraph, whereas moving to Text.Length leaves it collapsed. MarkdownSelectionFixtures.cs:406-412 inadvertently encodes this bug by calling Move(TextUnit.Paragraph, ...) directly on peer.Range(0, 0) without calling ExpandToEnclosingUnit(TextUnit.Paragraph) first.
findings.recommendation: Only apply UnitAt(MarkdownSelectionUnit.Paragraph, result.Start) in MarkdownSelectionRange.Move when the range being moved is non-degenerate (for example, _start != _end before moving / result.Start != result.End), and update MarkdownSelectionFixtures.cs:406-412 to call ExpandToEnclosingUnit(TextUnit.Paragraph) for non-empty paragraph movement while adding an assertion that moving peer.Range(0, 0) by TextUnit.Paragraph keeps the range degenerate.

findings.title: Cross-surface Shift+drag corrupts _pressSpan anchor when the document rebuilds mid-drag
findings.evidence: In OnPressed (lines 558-563), when Shift is held (_dragUnit == MarkdownSelectionUnit.Character), anchor is resolved from Document.Anchor, which can belong to an earlier or later surface than the clicked entry. Despite that, _pressLocalSpan is computed as new(_pressSpan.Start - entry.Start, _pressSpan.End - entry.Start) and _pressSurfaceIdentity is set to entry.Identity (the clicked surface). For example, if Entry[0] spans 0..16, Entry[1] spans 17..32, Document.Anchor is 2, and the user Shift+drags from offset 22 in Entry[1], _pressLocalSpan becomes (-15, -15) on Entry[1]. If streaming output or a visibility change triggers Refresh mid-drag (lines 331-339), Math.Clamp(_pressLocalSpan.Start, 0, pressedEntry.Text.Length) clamps -15 to 0 relative to Entry[1].Start (17), rewriting _pressSpan to (17, 17) and dropping the Entry[0] portion of the selection on the next UpdateDragSelection() call (line 212). Conversely, if the true anchor surface was removed while the clicked surface remained, pressedEntry is still found so StopDrag() is not called.
findings.recommendation: When _dragUnit == MarkdownSelectionUnit.Character, resolve the entry owning anchor (var anchorEntry = Document.EntryAt(anchor) ?? entry;) and record both _pressLocalSpan and _pressSurfaceIdentity against anchorEntry instead of the clicked entry.

findings.title: Visible collapsed caret is omitted from click-away and layout tracking, and _suppressCaret stays stuck on keyboard navigation
findings.evidence: DrawSelection() (lines 1167-1172) draws a collapsed caret whenever Document.Start == Document.End && !_suppressCaret && FocusState != FocusState.Unfocused && Document.Text.Length > 0, but three state transitions ignore this condition: (1) When ClearForClickAway() runs on a primary click to a non-focusable element (such as SelectionBlank Border or non-surface chrome), _suppressCaret is set to true (line 747) while WinUI keeps keyboard focus on MarkdownSelectionHost, so OnFocusChanged (lines 121-129) never fires; subsequent Left/Right/Up/Down/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown/Escape keys in HandleKey (lines 752-786) move Document.Caret without resetting _suppressCaret = false, leaving the caret invisible during keyboard navigation. (2) UpdateClickAwayRegistration() (lines 142-151) sets active to Document.Start != Document.End || _clicks.IsPending; once GetDoubleClickTime() expires after a single click (OnClickTimeout -> ResetClickSequence, line 153) or when a caret is placed by keyboard, the host unregisters from MarkdownSelectionClickAway while the caret is still drawn (and OnFocusChanged never updates click-away registration), so clicking a non-focusable blank area no longer hides the caret. (3) UpdateLayoutTracking() (lines 111-119) likewise omits the visible-caret condition, detaching LayoutUpdated while a collapsed caret is visible so scrolling an enclosing ScrollViewer/ScrollView leaves the caret overlay at stale coordinates.
findings.recommendation: Define a shared HasVisibleCaret predicate (Document.Start == Document.End && !_suppressCaret && FocusState != FocusState.Unfocused && Document.Text.Length > 0), include it in both UpdateLayoutTracking() and UpdateClickAwayRegistration(), call UpdateClickAwayRegistration() from OnFocusChanged and ClearForClickAway(), and set _suppressCaret = false in HandleKey when handling navigation/selection keys.

findings.title: InvalidateDocument subscribes to LayoutUpdated without scheduling layout, stalling metadata-only updates
findings.evidence: InvalidateDocument() (lines 99-109) sets _documentDirty = true and, when _loaded && !_trackingLayout && !_refreshPending, sets _refreshPending = true and attaches LayoutUpdated += OnLayout without calling InvalidateArrange(). In MarkdownSelectionHandler.Update (MarkdownTextSelection.cs:189-196), changes to marker.Metadata (oldEl.IsVisible != newEl.IsVisible, oldEl.Text != newEl.Text, oldEl.SeparatorAfter != newEl.SeparatorAfter, oldEl.IsLink != newEl.IsLink) mutate a plain CLR property and call marker.InvalidateEnclosingScope() without dirtying XAML Measure or Arrange (for example, toggling nested MarkdownTextSelection.Visibility(inner, ...) inside an already-open container or updating MarkdownTextSelection.Surface text on a fixed-size visual). Because no XAML layout pass is scheduled, OnLayout does not run: stale selection highlight rectangles stay rendered on _overlay, UIA TextPatternOnTextChanged / TextPatternOnTextSelectionChanged notifications are not raised, and idle hosts remain attached to LayoutUpdated until an unrelated layout occurs. (SemanticMessage in MarkdownSelectionFixtures.cs:128-140 masks this by calling selection.Refresh() explicitly.)
findings.recommendation: In InvalidateDocument(), when _loaded is true, set _refreshPending = true, call UpdateLayoutTracking(), and call InvalidateArrange() so WinUI schedules one coalesced layout pass that runs OnLayout even when _trackingLayout was already true or child layout did not change.

findings.title: Replacing a named keyframe leaves the old animation and trigger registered
findings.evidence: A configuration-only update from a looping `pulse` on Opacity to a `spin` on Rotation now reaches `Update`. `Reconciler.Update.cs:401–404` applies the new entries but only clears the old entries when the entire new array is null. The old opacity animation keeps running, and its `(UIElement, name)` entry remains in the static dictionary (`Reconciler.cs:6227–6248`). Unmount only removes names from the current declaration (`Reconciler.cs:4523–4524, 6357–6360`), so the old entry retains the control after unmount.
findings.recommendation: Diff keyframe entries by name, remove trigger records for dropped names, and stop their channels without interrupting surviving entries. Add a live test that replaces a looping entry and verifies cleanup after unmount.

findings.title: Removing a transition leaves it installed on the live control
findings.evidence: Rendering the same Border without `.OpacityTransition()` now declines the skip, but `Reconciler.Update.cs:380–382` does nothing when the new transition buckets are null. If only one transition is removed from a combined declaration, `ApplyTransitions` likewise only writes non-null channels (`Reconciler.cs:5553–5607`). The old XAML transition, compositor fallback, or theme transition collection remains active. The new fixture checks duration replacement, not removal (`AnimateModifierTests.cs:192–195`).
findings.recommendation: Pass both declarations to the transition updater and clear channels or collections that Reactor previously installed but that are now absent. Add live removal coverage for the XAML and compositor paths.

findings.title: Replacing a scroll binding leaves dropped properties animated
findings.evidence: A render that switches from `.ScrollLinked(... FadeOut(...))` to `.ScrollLinked(... ScaleRange(...))` now reaches `Update` without any other prop change. The non-null branch at `Reconciler.Update.cs:407–410` starts the new Scale expression but never stops the old Opacity expression; `ApplyScrollAnimation` only visits the new expressions (`Reconciler.cs:6383–6404`). The new scroll checks only assert the skip decision (`AnimateModifierTests.cs:197–205`).
findings.recommendation: Stop previously bound properties absent from the new declaration before applying the new expressions. Add a live selftest that changes the bound property and verifies that the old property no longer follows scroll.

findings.title: Removing `.Stagger()` leaves delays on retained children
findings.evidence: Removing `.Stagger()` from a stack with the same children now declines the skip, but `Reconciler.Update.cs:412–414` only handles a non-null new configuration. `ApplyStaggerDelays` writes `DelayTime` directly onto each child's installed animations (`Reconciler.cs:6195–6213`). A retained second child keeps its old delay even after the parent stops declaring stagger.
findings.recommendation: Restore the delays that Reactor overrode when stagger is removed. Add a live test that mounts a staggered panel, keeps its animated children unchanged, and verifies that removing the modifier restores the second child's delay.

findings.title: An implicit opacity animation can hide the loss of the named keyframe
findings.evidence: The check returns for any controller on `Opacity`, not just the controller it recorded. `ApplyPropertyAnimation` installs an implicit opacity animation for `.Animate(..., AnimateProperty.Opacity)`. Spec 066 §3 and Q4c establish that a XAML opacity push triggers that implicit animation, and §9.F establishes that implicit animations expose controllers. When the push replaces the named fade with the implicit animation, the check sees a non-null controller, clears the pending state, and never restores the fade.
findings.recommendation: Compare controller identity and distinguish a replacement caused by the initial XAML push from a deliberate newer owner. Add a mounted regression case combining an opacity keyframe, a nondefault base opacity, and an implicit opacity animation.

findings.title: A delayed commit check mistakes interrupted finite fades for completed ones
findings.evidence: The stopwatch starts when Reactor queues the animation, not when the compositor starts playing it. If XAML cancels a finite fade in its first frame and the UI thread does not run the check until after the declared duration, the guard classifies the fade as completed even though XAML stopped it before it could play. The new tests use a 60-second finite fade and a 1 ms fade with a competing opacity push; neither distinguishes actual completion from an early stop observed late.
findings.recommendation: Track whether the initial push interrupted playback rather than inferring completion from elapsed time at the callback. Test an interrupted finite fade with delayed observation, and verify natural completion separately without a competing opacity write.

findings.title: The pending check can undo an explicit stop even without a XAML opacity change
findings.evidence: Every opacity keyframe arms the check, even on a rendered element whose opacity has not changed. If application code calls `visual.StopAnimation("Opacity")` before the pending check runs, the trigger entry and `KeyframeOpacityCheck` still match, but the current controller is null. For a looping fade, the check then starts it again. Nothing in this path verifies that XAML pushed an opacity value.
findings.recommendation: Require evidence of a pending or observed XAML opacity push before replaying. Add a rendered-element test that starts and explicitly stops a looping opacity keyframe without changing its base opacity.

findings.title: Cancelled opacity checks leave layout subscriptions attached
findings.evidence: The `LayoutUpdated` delegate captures the element, visual, animation, and controller. It is stored only in a local variable and can detach itself only on a later layout notification. Modifier replacement and pool cleanup merely clear `KeyframeOpacityCheck`, and keyframe removal deletes the trigger entry. If the element is removed after the subscription is installed and there is no subsequent layout, cancellation leaves the delegate registered. `ElementPool.CancelOpacitySync` explicitly detaches its analogous layout subscription on unmount for this reason.
findings.recommendation: Store the pending layout delegate in the attached state and detach it when the keyframe is superseded or removed, when the element unmounts, and when it returns to the pool.

findings.title: The deferred-reset fixture expects a later style push to preserve the fade
findings.evidence: The fixture waits for the initial push, pauses the named fade at progress 0.5, then clears the local opacity of 0.4 and exposes the style value of 0.65. The newly added commit wait gives XAML time to push that changed value after the one-shot check has already been consumed. The assertion nevertheless requires the same paused controller to survive, contrary to the changelog's stated behavior for subsequent XAML opacity changes.
findings.recommendation: Check deferred ownership before the later XAML push, or use an unchanged effective opacity for the ownership-only case. Test separately that a subsequent effective style-opacity change stops the fade without replaying it.

findings.title: The commit helper silently proceeds on timeout or failure
findings.evidence: `Task.WhenAny` returns the winning task, but `AfterNextCommit` neither checks which task won nor awaits the commit task itself. A timeout or fault therefore looks like a successful commit. In particular, the off-tree cases can attach the element without establishing that the first commit completed while it was detached, so they can pass without exercising the intended layout-wait branch.
findings.recommendation: Await the commit task with a bounded timeout that fails the fixture on timeout or fault. For detached and collapsed cases, verify that the check entered the layout-wait phase before making the element visible.
