findings.title: Moving a UI Automation caret by paragraph turns it into a selection
findings.evidence: MarkdownSelectionRangeMovement.Move deliberately returns equal endpoints when moving a degenerate range. The new paragraph branch replaces those endpoints with the entire destination surface. For example, moving an insertion point at the start of the first paragraph by one paragraph now returns the full second paragraph instead of a caret at its start. The new selftest at MarkdownSelectionFixtures.cs:406–412 starts with a degenerate range and asserts the expanded result.
findings.recommendation: Keep the moved result degenerate when the input range was degenerate. Test paragraph navigation with both a caret and a nondegenerate range, including that the latter excludes the surface separator.

findings.title: A document update can move the fixed end of a character drag
findings.evidence: After Document.Rebuild remaps the existing selection, Refresh separately reconstructs the drag anchor from a saved offset in the pressed surface. UpdateDragSelection then overwrites the remapped anchor with that offset. A prefix inserted before the mouse-down point in the same surface leaves the saved offset pointing at the wrong text. A Shift-drag that started with its anchor in an earlier paragraph is worse: the negative local offset is clamped to zero, moving the anchor to the start of the pressed paragraph even if that paragraph did not change.
findings.recommendation: Use the document's remapped anchor for character drags. For word and surface drags, remap both saved press endpoints against the old and new surface text rather than just clamping the old offsets.

findings.title: Click-away stops working for a visible caret after the double-click timeout
findings.evidence: A single text click leaves a collapsed range and draws a caret. Once the timer clears _clicks.IsPending, UpdateClickAwayRegistration unregisters the host even though it still has focus and DrawSelection still shows the caret. A later click on a non-focusable blank area that leaves focus unchanged therefore never calls ClearForClickAway. This contradicts the guide's promise to clear the collapsed selection on an outside primary click.
findings.recommendation: Keep click-away registered while the host displays a caret, independently of the multiclick timer. Add a real-input case that waits for the timer to expire before clicking a non-focusable target and checks that the caret disappears without consuming the click.

findings.title: A focused caret stops tracking layout when the mouse is released
findings.evidence: UpdateLayoutTracking ignores a focused, collapsed selection once the pointer is released, but DrawSelection still puts a rectangle in the overlay at the old caret coordinates. For example, resizing a nonselectable spacer above the paragraph moves the paragraph without changing the selection marker's size, visibility, or metadata. None of the new invalidation hooks runs, so the caret stays at its old position until another action refreshes the host.
findings.recommendation: Track layout while a caret is visible, or add a geometry invalidation path that observes position-only changes. Cover a focused caret through a layout change that moves its surface without resizing it.

findings.title: Document-order hit testing defeats the existing distance pruning
findings.evidence: The old hit test visited surfaces in increasing order of their bounding-box distance and stopped when the next surface could not beat the best glyph. The new loop visits surfaces in document order. During a drag near the bottom of a long message, each successive paragraph above the pointer can be closer than the last, so the loop walks the glyphs of most preceding paragraphs before reaching the nearby one. That work now runs on pointer moves and drag-scroll ticks.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the nearest-first pruning without restoring per-move LINQ allocations: find and scan the nearest surface first, then scan only other surfaces whose bound can beat that result. Verify glyph visits for a hit near the end of a long message.

findings.title: Triple-click makes the existing Ctrl+A assertions pass without Ctrl+A
findings.evidence: The test now selects all of "inner text" with triple-click immediately before pressing Ctrl+A. The range assertion can therefore pass if Ctrl+A does nothing, and receivedSelection.Contains("inner text") can be satisfied by the triple-click event already in the queue. The clipboard check proves Ctrl+C copied the selection, not that Ctrl+A made it.
findings.recommendation: Before sending Ctrl+A, establish a collapsed or partial range, record the event baseline, and require both a new selection-change event and the transition to the full range.

findings.title: RunFocusedContainerCheck misclassifies live on-screen shifted rows as stale on multi-row moves, stealing focus and leaving the newly focused row unwatched
findings.evidence: In `RunFocusedContainerCheck` (`ElementFactory.StaleContainers.cs:80-96`), when `index != expected`, the code decides `child` is still shown in its right place only if another realized control in `_keyByControl.Keys` currently has `repeater.GetElementIndex(control) == index`. That held in `FocusedRowSwappedOnScreenThenScrolled_NoStaleRow` only by coincidence because `Swap2And3` (`KeyedListDiff` emitting `Source.Move(3, 2)`) shifts a single row whose old index `2` equals `newIndex = 2`. For any move spanning multiple rows—e.g. `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, ...] -> [0, 4, 1, 2, 3, ...]` (`Source.Move(4, 1)`) while row `"2"` is focused on screen, or `Source.Move(100, 0)` while scrolled to focused row `"50"`—old `"4"` is recycled (`RecycleElement` removes it from `_keyByControl`) and `"4"` is realized at `newIndex = 1` (`GetElementIndex == 1`, colliding only with `"1"`). Live on-screen row `"2"` now sits at `expected = 3` with `GetElementIndex == 2`, and no other control in `_keyByControl` has `GetElementIndex == 2`. `RunFocusedContainerCheck` therefore calls `MoveFocusOffStaleContainer` immediately: (1) it steals keyboard focus from the user's active on-screen row `"2"` onto neighbor `"1"` or `"3"`, and (2) if focus lands on `"3"` (`GetElementIndex == 3`, `expected = 4`), `"3"` also carries a stale repeater index without `WatchFocusedContainer` armed, so scrolling away and back pins `"3"` at stale index `3` and still corrupts rows.
findings.recommendation: Replace the duplicate-`GetElementIndex` scan with a direct check of whether `child` is still the live visible container for an existing item—i.e. `expected >= 0 && _controlByKey.TryGetValue(key, out var live) && ReferenceEquals(live, child)` and `child`'s bounds still intersect `FindViewport(repeater)`—arming `WatchFocusedContainer(repeater, fe)` while it stays in view and calling `MoveFocusOffStaleContainer` only once the row was removed (`expected < 0`), superseded (`!ReferenceEquals(live, child)`), or scrolled out of the viewport into the pinned pool. Update the matching prose in `docs/specs/042-keyed-list-reconciliation-design.md` line 180 accordingly.

findings.title: Focusing a shifted row after a Move bypasses stale-container tracking and still corrupts rows on scroll
findings.evidence: `ElementFactory<T>.RefreshRealizedItems` (`ElementFactory.cs:375-379`) calls `ScheduleFocusedContainerCheck` only when `_listState.PinnedIndicesMayBeStale` is set by `Move`, `Remove`, or `Reset`, and `RunFocusedContainerCheck` (`ElementFactory.StaleContainers.cs:67-78`) runs once on `LayoutUpdated` and exits if `FindFocusedChild(repeater)` is `null` or has `index == expected`. Because WinUI `ItemsRepeater` never repairs shifted `GetElementIndex` values after a `Move`, all shifted rows keep stale indices indefinitely. In normal user flows—such as clicking an external "Sort" or "Move up" button with pointer/keyboard (which moves focus to that button before `Move` runs, unlike `Harness.ClickButton`'s UIA `IInvokeProvider.Invoke()` in `RepeaterStaleIndexFixtures.cs:152`) or holding focus on unshifted row `0` (`index == expected`) during `Swap2And3`—`RunFocusedContainerCheck` finds no mismatched focused child and disarms without watching anything. If the user then clicks or tabs onto shifted row `"2"` (`GetElementIndex == 2`, `expected == 3`), scrolls away so `ItemsRepeater` pins it, and scrolls back, no check or `EffectiveViewportChanged` watch ever runs and `ItemsRepeater` hands the pinned row back at stale index `2`, duplicating `"2"` and dropping `"3"`.
findings.recommendation: Track on `ElementFactory<T>` / `ReactorListState` whether the repeater has un-reset `Move` index drift, and subscribe to `repeater.GotFocus` (or keep a `GotFocus` handler on keyed repeaters) so whenever focus enters a repeater child whose `repeater.GetElementIndex(child)` differs from `_listState.ByKey[key].Index`, `WatchFocusedContainer` / `ScheduleFocusedContainerCheck` is armed for that container.

findings.title: MoveFocusOffStaleContainer leaves the stale row focused and pinned when no sibling row in the repeater can take focus
findings.evidence: `MoveFocusOffStaleContainer` (`ElementFactory.StaleContainers.cs:114-131`) only builds candidates from other realized controls in `_keyByControl` and returns after trying `control.Focus(state)` on each. When a list containing a focused/pinned row (e.g. at index `2`) is cleared or filtered to empty (`Source.Clear()` or removing all rows), or when remaining realized rows contain no focusable elements (e.g. display-only rows while only the removed/moved active row had a `Button` or `TextBox`), `candidates` is empty or every `control.Focus(state)` returns `false`. Focus stays on `stale`, keeping it pinned in `ItemsRepeater` at `staleIndex = 2` (and still referenced in `_controlByKey`, since `ElementFactory.cs:405` only removes `key` from `_mountedElements`). When items are later added back via `NotifyCollectionChangedAction.Add`—which `ReactorListState.cs:153-155` intentionally excludes from setting `PinnedIndicesMayBeStale`—`ItemsRepeater` hands the stale deleted row back for index `2` without calling `GetElement`.
findings.recommendation: If no sibling row in `candidates` accepts focus, fall back to moving focus outside `stale` (for example via `FocusManager.TryMoveFocus(FocusNavigationDirection.Next)` / `Previous` or focusing an enclosing focusable `Control` such as the ancestor `ScrollViewer` or host root with `FocusState.Programmatic`) so `ItemsRepeater` drops the pin. Also remove `key` from `_controlByKey` when dropping a removed row in `ElementFactory.cs:405` if `_controlByKey` still points to the removed row's control.

findings.title: Selftest fixtures omit the Reset path entirely and do not assert on-screen focus retention before scrolling
findings.evidence: First, `ReactorListState.cs:139,147-156`, `ElementFactory.StaleContainers.cs:14,20`, and `docs/specs/042-keyed-list-reconciliation-design.md:180` explicitly claim `Reset` is handled alongside `Move` and `Remove`, and `ReactorListStateTests.cs:145` unit-tests the `PinnedIndicesMayBeStale` flag on `Source.Clear()`, but `RepeaterStaleIndexFixtures.cs:192-250` only exercises `Swap2And3`, `Move2ToTop`, `Remove2`, and `Move2ToEnd`—never `Reset` (`KeyedListDiff` >25% churn bailout or clearing to empty and repopulating). Second, `FocusedRowSwappedOnScreenThenScrolled_NoStaleRow` (`lines 243-250`) states in its comment that "A focused row reordered on screen keeps focus", yet `RunAsync` (`lines 162-176`) guards its focus checks with `if (target is not null && s.ChangeWhileScrolledAway)` and scrolls away immediately without verifying that `target` kept focus after the on-screen reorder; it also tests only an adjacent 2-row swap and uses `Harness.ClickButton` (`lines 152, 179`), which invokes UIA `IInvokeProvider` without transferring focus away from the row like a real button click.
findings.recommendation: Add selftest fixtures in `RepeaterStaleIndexFixtures.cs` (and register them in `SelfTestFixtureRegistry.cs`) covering: (1) `Reset` with a focused/pinned row via both >25% churn bailout (e.g. `k.Reverse()`) and clearing to empty then re-adding items, (2) a multi-row on-screen move (e.g. moving index `4` to `1` while row `2` is focused) asserting `ReferenceEquals(FocusManager.GetFocusedElement(target.XamlRoot), target)` before scrolling, and (3) focusing a shifted row after an unfocused reorder and scrolling away and back.

findings.title: ApplyModifiers and ClearInteractionStates ignore active Background/Foreground interaction overrides, clobbering hover visuals and re-pinning stale local brushes over ThemeRef
findings.evidence: This change refactors InteractionStateTracker for Background and Foreground onto ApplyInteractionBrush (Reconciler.cs:6086-6091, 6258-6265, 6304-6338) with BackgroundOverrideApplied/ForegroundOverrideApplied and NormalBackground/NormalForeground, but unlike BorderBrush immediately above in ApplyModifiers (Reconciler.cs:7265-7272), ApplyModifiers (lines 7340-7363) never checks _interactionTrackers before writing or clearing Background/Foreground, and ClearInteractionStates (lines 6127-6137) drops the tracker without restoring active state overrides. Concrete failures: (1) Any non-skipped re-render while PointerOver/Pressed is active on an element using .Background("#RRGGBB") or changing brushA -> brushB satisfies !ReferenceEquals(m.Background, oldM?.Background) and immediately overwrites the active hover/pressed brush on fe while leaving tracker.NormalBackground stale; if the user then clicks (Pressed) before pointer-exit, ApplyInteractionBrush sees overrideApplied == true (lines 6311-6320), skips recapturing brushB, and restores stale brushA on pointer-exit. (2) If an element transitions from .Background(localBrush) to .Background(ThemeRef) while hovered, ApplyModifiers (lines 7347-7352) clears BackgroundProperty mid-hover while leaving BackgroundOverrideApplied == true and NormalBackground == localBrush; pressing (PointerOver -> Pressed -> PointerOver -> Normal) re-writes activeBrush without recapturing normalLocal and then writes the removed localBrush back via fe.SetValue(dp, normal) (line 6335), permanently shadowing the {ThemeResource} Style. (3) Removing .InteractionStates(...) while hovered leaves the hover brush permanently set as a local value over any ThemeRef Style because ClearInteractionStates (lines 6127-6137) never restores or clears active overrides.
findings.recommendation: Mirror BorderBrush's active-override guard (lines 7265-7272) for Background (lines 7340-7352) and Foreground (lines 7355-7363): when tracker.BackgroundOverrideApplied / tracker.ForegroundOverrideApplied is true, update tracker.NormalBackground / tracker.NormalForeground (to the new Brush or DependencyProperty.UnsetValue when cleared) without overwriting the live interaction brush on fe. Also update ClearInteractionStates (lines 6127-6137) to transition any active Background, Foreground, and BorderBrush overrides back to Normal before removing the tracker.

findings.title: ApplyThemeBindings leaves the previous render's themed Style active when all current ThemeRef keys are unrepresentable or XamlReader.Load fails
findings.evidence: Reconciler.Update.cs:158-161 only calls ClearThemeBindings(thFe) when oldEl.ThemeBindings is not null && newEl.ThemeBindings is null; whenever newEl.ThemeBindings is non-empty it calls ApplyThemeBindings(thFe, newEl.ThemeBindings). Inside ApplyThemeBindings, if every binding in newEl.ThemeBindings is rejected by FormatThemeResourceReference (lines 8401-8405), line 8408 executes `if (setters.Length == 0) return;` without calling ClearThemeBindings(fe) (and likewise on `targetType is null` at line 8375 or `XamlReader.Load` throwing at lines 8422-8429). Counterexample: a TextBlock mounted with `.Foreground(new ThemeRef("ValidBrush"))` (or `.Background(ValidA).Foreground(ValidB)`) that updates in-place to `.Foreground(new ThemeRef(""))` logs that the property "is left unset" (line 8592), yet fe.Style and ReactorAppliedThemeStyleProperty still hold the previous render's synthesized Style, keeping ValidBrush (and any removed sibling binding ValidA) applied on the control.
findings.recommendation: Call ClearThemeBindings(fe) before returning when targetType is null (line 8375), when setters.Length == 0 (line 8408), and inside the XamlReader.Load catch block (line 8428) so stale Reactor-owned themed Styles are removed and any base Style in ReactorThemeBaseStyleProperty is restored.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for unrepresentable ThemeRef runtime handling/warning emission and mid-hover Background/Foreground re-renders

No unit test or selftest mounts/updates an element with an unrepresentable ThemeRef alongside a valid ThemeRef, transitions valid -> unrepresentable on update, or subscribes via ReactorTrace.Subscribe to assert single-shot DiagnosticLog.Warning emission (unlike NamedStyleResolutionFixture.cs:182-273). (2) InteractionStatesRestoresCurrentExplicitBrush (ThemeRefStyleFixtures.cs:202-244) exits hover at line 225 before calling setSecond!(true) at line 234, so unlike PanelBorderFixture.cs:88-149 (UpdateDuringHover / ChangeDuringHover / ClearDuringHover), no test re-renders Background or Foreground while PointerOver/Pressed is active.
findings.recommendation: Add selftest cases in ThemeRefStyleFixtures covering: (a) an element with one valid and one unrepresentable ThemeRef (verifying the valid setter still applies, a subsequent update to only an unrepresentable key clears the prior themed Style, and DiagnosticLog.Warning fires once per bad key via ReactorTrace.Subscribe), and (b) re-rendering Background/Foreground (brush change and Brush -> ThemeRef transition) while InteractionStates is in PointerOver and Pressed.

findings.title: WarnUnrepresentableThemeKey retains unbounded key strings in _warnedThemeKeys and emits unsanitized control characters into diagnostic logs
findings.evidence: Reconciler.cs:8576-8577 notes that _warnedThemeKeys caps what "a data-driven caller could retain", but WarnUnrepresentableThemeKey (lines 8578-8593) bounds only key count (WarnedThemeKeysCap = 256) with no per-key length limit and interpolates raw `key` directly into DiagnosticLog.Warning. By contrast, the companion warning helper ElementExtensions.WarnUnresolvedStyle (src/Reactor/Elements/ElementExtensions.cs:783-808, per Spec 044 §6.2.1) truncates keys to MaxKeyChars = 256 before deduplication and logging. Because FormatThemeResourceReference (lines 8564-8565) specifically routes keys containing '\r', '\n', '\t', or disallowed control characters into WarnUnrepresentableThemeKey, data-driven callers can pin up to 256 arbitrarily large strings in the static _warnedThemeKeys dictionary for the process lifetime and inject raw multi-line breaks into DebugWarning / TraceListener output.
findings.recommendation: Follow Spec 044 §6.2.1 as in ElementExtensions.WarnUnresolvedStyle: truncate keys exceeding MaxKeyChars = 256 before inserting into _warnedThemeKeys, and sanitize or escape control characters ('\r', '\n', '\t', and XML-invalid chars) before formatting the DiagnosticLog.Warning message.

findings.title: BuildCacheKey uses unescaped '|' and '=' delimiters, allowing newly-supported quoted ThemeRef keys to collide in _styleCache and _basedStyleCache
findings.evidence: FormatThemeResourceReference (Reconciler.cs:8555-8574) expands ThemeRef support to arbitrary XAML-quotable resource keys, including keys containing '|' and '='. However, BuildCacheKey (lines 643-654) still concatenates `sb.Append('|').Append(key).Append('=').Append(bindings[key].ResourceKey)` without escaping or length-prefixing ResourceKey, and both _styleCache (line 8377) and _basedStyleCache (line 8439) look up compiled Styles solely by this string. Counterexample: `Button("A").Background(new ThemeRef("X|Foreground=Y"))` and `Button("B").Background(new ThemeRef("X")).Foreground(new ThemeRef("Y"))` produce the identical cache key `"Button|Background=X|Foreground=Y"`, causing the second element to receive a cached Style with the wrong setter set.
findings.recommendation: Length-prefix each resource key in BuildCacheKey (for example, `sb.Append('|').Append(key).Append('=').Append(resourceKey.Length).Append(':').Append(resourceKey)`) and add a collision regression case with '|' and '=' in ReconcilerCacheKeyTests.cs.

findings.title: ReactorAppliedThemeStyleProperty and ReactorThemeBaseStyleProperty remain attached when ElementPool.CleanElement resets pooled controls
findings.evidence: ApplyStyleToElement (Reconciler.cs:8658-8662) stores both the synthesized Style (ReactorAppliedThemeStyleProperty) and any author baseStyle (ReactorThemeBaseStyleProperty, lines 615-620) as attached DependencyProperties on the FrameworkElement. When a pooled control (Button, TextBlock, Border, Grid, StackPanel) unmounts, ElementPool.CleanElement (src/Reactor/Core/ElementPool.cs:308-309) executes `if (fe.Style is not null) fe.ClearValue(FrameworkElement.StyleProperty);` without calling Reconciler.ClearThemeBindings(fe) or clearing those two attached DPs. Any component-constructed Style (including custom ControlTemplates or object graphs not retained by _basedStyleCache once BasedStyleCacheCap = 256 is reached) stays rooted on the pooled FrameworkElement across idle pooling and subsequent un-themed rentals.
findings.recommendation: Update ElementPool.CleanElement (ElementPool.cs:308-309) to call Reconciler.ClearThemeBindings(fe) (or explicitly ClearValue both ReactorAppliedThemeStyleProperty and ReactorThemeBaseStyleProperty alongside FrameworkElement.StyleProperty) and update PoolResetSetConsistencyTests accordingly.

findings.title: Styling guide and template claim ThemeRef layers onto 'any Style you set', omitting that custom subclass Style TargetTypes silently drop ThemeRef
findings.evidence: docs/guide/styling.md:325-327 and its source template docs/_pipeline/templates/styling.md.dt:201-203 state unconditionally: "A `ThemeRef` modifier such as `.Foreground(Theme.PrimaryText)` layers on top of a named style (or any Style you set) rather than replacing it." However, GetExactStyleTargetType (Reconciler.cs:8512-8520) only emits unprefixed type names in `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls` or `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.Primitives`; for any custom subclass (such as Reactor's own `FlexPanel` or a `[GenerateReactorWrapper]` custom control styled with `TargetType="local:MyControl"`), GetStyleTargetType walks up to `Panel`/`Control`, WinUI rejects `style.BasedOn = baseStyle` because a base-type Style cannot inherit from a derived-type Style, and TryApplyBasedStyle (lines 8459-8462) catches the failure and leaves `fe.Style = baseStyle` with the ThemeRef silently ignored. Additionally, shipped skill doc skills/design-docs/theme-aware-resources.md:9 still states that mounting/updating an element with a ThemeRef resolves brushes by walking ThemeDictionaries rather than synthesizing a {ThemeResource} Style.
findings.recommendation: Qualify the prose in docs/_pipeline/templates/styling.md.dt and docs/guide/styling.md to note that BasedOn layering applies to Styles targeting built-in WinUI Controls/Primitives types (custom subclass TargetTypes retain the author Style without the ThemeRef setter), and update skills/design-docs/theme-aware-resources.md:9 to accurately describe the {ThemeResource} Style + BasedOn pipeline.

findings.title: Configuration-only removals and channel narrowings now enter Reconciler.Update but leave ImplicitTransitions, ThemeTransitions, StaggerConfig, and dropped Keyframe/Scroll channels active
findings.evidence: src/Reactor/Core/Element.cs:519 widens ShallowEquals (and CanSkipUpdate at Element.cs:481) from AnimationConfig to all 10 AnimationExtras fields so configuration-only updates and removals enter Reconciler.Update, as asserted for `cleared` in tests/Reactor.Tests/AnimationExtrasEqualityTests.cs:27-39 and AnimateModifierTests.cs:204 and promised in CHANGELOG.md:62-64. Unlike AnimationConfig (which clears dropped flags at Reconciler.Update.cs:214-222), several newly-routed animation extras lack corresponding clear/narrow paths on in-place update: (1) lines 376-377 guard `ApplyTransitions` on `newEl.ImplicitTransitions is not null || newEl.ThemeTransitions is not null` with no `else` clear branch, and Reconciler.cs:5552-5648 only assigns non-null sub-properties, so updating `Border(child).OpacityTransition(800ms)` to `Border(child)`, removing `.WithTransitions(...)`/`.ItemContainerTransitions(...)`, or narrowing `.OpacityTransition().ScaleTransition()` to `.OpacityTransition()` leaves `UIElement.*Transition`, `*Transitions`, or compositor `visual.ImplicitAnimations` permanently attached; (2) lines 413-414 guard `ApplyStaggerDelays` on `newEl.StaggerConfig is not null` with no `oldEl.StaggerConfig is not null` reset, leaving skipped children's `ImplicitAnimations[*].DelayTime` at `oldDelay * i` when `.Stagger(...)` is removed; (3) lines 402-410 only call `ClearKeyframeAnimations`/`ClearScrollAnimation` when the whole property becomes null, so dropping one named `.Keyframes(...)` entry from a chained element leaves its `(target, name)` trigger cached in `_keyframeTriggerValues` and any looping channel running, and dropping an expression from `.ScrollLinked(...)` never calls `visual.StopAnimation` for the removed property.
findings.recommendation: Update Reconciler.Update.cs:375-414 to diff `oldEl` against `newEl` for each animation extra: add a transition update/clear path when `oldEl.ImplicitTransitions` or `oldEl.ThemeTransitions` was non-null (nulling cleared XAML `*Transition`/`*Transitions` properties or removing outgoing compositor `ImplicitAnimations` keys while preserving channels owned by `LayoutAnimation`/`AnimationConfig`), reset child `ImplicitAnimations[*].DelayTime` to `TimeSpan.Zero` when `oldEl.StaggerConfig is not null && newEl.StaggerConfig is null`, and remove/stop outgoing `KeyframeEntry` names and `ScrollExpression` target properties that were present in `oldEl` but omitted in `newEl`.

findings.title: Delegating ShallowEquals directly to synthesized AnimationExtras.Equals breaks steady-state skipping and re-applies animations every render for .Keyframes(), .ScrollLinked(), and .OpacityTransition()
findings.evidence: Element.ShallowEquals (src/Reactor/Core/Element.cs:501-527) exists specifically to perform structural comparison where default record equality falls back to reference equality, using `AttachedEqual`, `ThemeBindingsEqual`, `ResourceOverridesEqual`, and `ContextValuesEqual` at lines 520-526 for the other `ElementExtras` slots. Line 519 instead calls `(a.Extensions?.Animations ?? default).Equals(b.Extensions?.Animations ?? default)`, where `KeyframeEntry[]`/`KeyframeFrame[]`, `ScrollExpression[]`, and WinUI's `ScalarTransition`/`Vector3Transition`/`BrushTransition` compare by reference. Because the fluent modifiers `.Keyframes(...)`, `.ScrollLinked(...)`, `.OpacityTransition(duration)`, `.RotationTransition(duration)`, `.BackgroundTransition(duration)`, and parameterless `.ScaleTransition()`/`.TranslationTransition()` unconditionally allocate fresh arrays or transition wrappers on every call (src/Reactor/Elements/ElementExtensions.cs:2707-2760, 3310-3342), elements using them (including `OpacityDemo` and `KeyframeDemo` in docs/_pipeline/apps/animation/App.cs:24,120,331) can no longer skip on unrelated parent re-renders. For `.ScrollLinked(...)`, `ApplyScrollAnimation` (src/Reactor/Core/Reconciler.cs:6383-6397) has no idempotency guard, so every unrelated re-render now allocates fresh compositor `ExpressionAnimation` instances and calls `visual.StartAnimation(...)`; for `.OpacityTransition(...)`, `ApplyTransitions` replaces the live transition/implicit animation on every render.
findings.recommendation: Follow the `AttachedEqual`/`ThemeBindingsEqual`/`ResourceOverridesEqual`/`ContextValuesEqual` pattern at src/Reactor/Core/Element.cs:520-526 by introducing an `AnimationsEqual(in AnimationExtras a, in AnimationExtras b)` helper for `ShallowEquals` that compares `KeyframeEntry[]`/`KeyframeFrame[]` and `ScrollExpression[]` element-by-element via `AsSpan().SequenceEqual(...)` (`KeyframeFrame` and `ScrollExpression` are already `readonly record struct`s) and compares `ImplicitTransitions` channels by `Duration` (plus `Components` on `Vector3Transition`), keeping reference equality only for arbitrary `ThemeTransitions` (`Xaml.Media.Animation.Transition`) instances.

findings.title: ExtrasAcrossUpdates taints the control before testing OpacityTransition, omits transition removal, and never verifies equal-config skipping in direct or child-skip modes
findings.evidence: In `AnimateModifierTests.ExtrasAcrossUpdates` (lines 156-212, registered as both `Animate_ExtrasAcrossUpdates` and `Animate_ExtrasChildSkip`): (1) line 163 mounts `.LayoutAnimation(...)` and line 172 calls `ElementCompositionPreview.GetElementVisual(border)` on the same `Border` reused at lines 191-194 for `.OpacityTransition(...)`; that permanently compositor-taints `border`, causing `ApplyTransitions` (src/Reactor/Core/Reconciler.cs:5560) to throw `UnauthorizedAccessException` and take `ApplyTransitionsViaCompositor`, leaving normal untainted XAML `UIElement.OpacityTransition` updates untested; (2) lines 185-189 test mount, change, and removal (`Update(Border(child))`) for `LayoutAnimation`, whereas lines 191-194 test 200ms -> 800ms for `OpacityTransition` and stop without testing `Update(Border(child))`, missing that `Reconciler.Update` never clears removed transitions; (3) unlike `ConfigurationAcrossUpdates` right above it (lines 124-133), `ExtrasAcrossUpdates` never updates with an equal configuration to assert `reconciler.DebugElementsSkipped` increments, never asserts `ReferenceEquals(((StackPanel)root).Children[0], border)` when `childSkip` is true, and emits the duplicate check name `name + "_SameControl"` four times.
findings.recommendation: Test `.OpacityTransition(...)` on a fresh untainted control (checking `border.OpacityTransition?.Duration`) in addition to the compositor-tainted fallback, add the `Update(Border(child))` removal check for transitions (plus update/removal coverage for `StaggerConfig` and `ThemeTransitions`), assert `reconciler.DebugElementsSkipped` increments on an equal-configuration update in both direct and `childSkip` modes, verify `ReferenceEquals(((StackPanel)root).Children[0], ...)` when `childSkip` is true, and pass step suffixes to `Update(...)` so each TAP check name is unique.

findings.title: ImplicitTransitions theory case duplicates `cleared` for `changed` and claims WinUI selftest coverage for native transition values that does not exist
findings.evidence: In `AnimationExtrasEqualityTests.Values(nameof(Element.ImplicitTransitions))` (lines 76-78), `changedValue` is `null`, so `changed` (`WithValue(property, changedValue)` at line 25) is identical to `cleared` (`WithValue(property, null)` at line 26) and both `firstValue` and `equalValue` are empty `new ImplicitTransitions()` records with all transition channels null. findings.title: Animation guide implies callers can avoid fresh objects/arrays in .OpacityTransition(), .Keyframes(), and .ScrollLinked(), which have no such overloads
findings.evidence: docs/_pipeline/templates/animation.md.dt:46-50 (and compiled docs/guide/animation.md:33-37) states: "Native objects and arrays use reference equality: rebuilding `.OpacityTransition()`, `.WithTransitions()`, `.Keyframes()`, or `.ScrollLinked()` with fresh objects or arrays prevents skipping, even when the settings match." In src/Reactor/Elements/ElementExtensions.cs (and skills/reactor.api.txt:646,707,727,761), only `.WithTransitions(params Transition[] transitions)` (along with `.ItemContainerTransitions(...)` and `.ScaleTransition(Vector3Transition?)`/`.TranslationTransition(Vector3Transition?)`) accepts caller-supplied arrays or native transition objects. `.OpacityTransition(TimeSpan? duration = null)` (ElementExtensions.cs:2707-2715) unconditionally allocates `new ScalarTransition()` internally, `.Keyframes(...)` (ElementExtensions.cs:3310-3325) unconditionally allocates `KeyframeEntry[]` and `KeyframeFrame[]` internally, and `.ScrollLinked(...)` (ElementExtensions.cs:3335-3342) unconditionally allocates `ScrollExpression[]` internally—callers cannot pass cached objects or arrays to those three modifiers.
findings.recommendation: If `ShallowEquals` keeps reference equality for arrays and native transitions, revise docs/_pipeline/templates/animation.md.dt:46-50 (and recompile docs/guide/animation.md via `Reactor.DocPipeline`) to distinguish modifiers that accept reusable instances/arrays (`.WithTransitions()`, `.ItemContainerTransitions()`, `.ScaleTransition(transition)`, `.TranslationTransition(transition)`) from modifiers that always allocate per call (`.OpacityTransition()`, `.RotationTransition()`, `.BackgroundTransition()`, `.Keyframes()`, `.ScrollLinked()`), where skipping requires reusing/memoizing the element or setting the record properties directly; if structural comparison is added to `ShallowEquals`, update both the template/guide and CHANGELOG.md:64-65 accordingly.

findings.title: Replacing the last valid ThemeRef with a rejected key leaves the old theme brush applied
findings.evidence: If a mounted element changes from a valid Foreground ThemeRef to a key containing both quote characters, the formatter rejects the new setter and the zero-setter branch returns without clearing the old synthesized Style. Reconciler.Update.cs:164–168 only clears that Style when ThemeBindings becomes null; here it is still non-null. The warning says the property is left unset, but the element continues to show the old resource.
findings.recommendation: When no setters survive, clear the previously owned theme Style through ClearThemeBindings so the author base is preserved. Add a live update fixture for valid-to-rejected and check that the old brush is gone.

findings.title: Quoted resource keys can alias different bindings in the style cache
findings.evidence: BuildCacheKey at lines 643–653 concatenates unescaped property names and resource keys with `|` and `=`. A Button with Background key `Accent|Foreground=Text` and one with Background key `Accent` plus Foreground key `Text` both produce `Button|Background=Accent|Foreground=Text`. The new quoting path accepts the first key, but either cache can return the other binding set's compiled Style before the formatter runs. Controls sharing the same author base are affected too.
findings.recommendation: Use a structural cache key or length-prefix each field. Add a unit test showing that these two binding sets produce different keys while preserving order independence.

findings.title: A hover-to-press transition can restore a brush superseded by a re-render
findings.evidence: Start with an explicit brush A, enter hover, then re-render with brush B while still hovered. ApplyModifiers writes B at lines 7339–7343. If the pointer then presses, the state-brush branch overwrites B but does not recapture it because overrideApplied is already true. On exit, the local brush matches the last interaction write and the helper restores A. The new explicit-brush fixture changes the brush only between separate hovers, so it misses this sequence.
findings.recommendation: Before each state-brush write, check whether the local value still matches the last interaction write. If another writer replaced it, capture that new local value as the baseline. Add a fixture that re-renders between hover and press.

findings.title: A missing or shadowed SplitView base falls back to the unsafe Style path
findings.evidence: The new lookup treats `DefaultSplitViewStyle` as optional, but the comment and SplitView fixture identify it as necessary for Style changes on a loaded SplitView. ResourceLookup.TryFind returns false if a higher-priority application resource with that key is not a Style. In that case ApplyThemeBindings proceeds without a base: the first rejected write can be swallowed after caching the Style, and the next cache hit at lines 8383–8386 retries the write outside the catch.

findings.title: Rejected ThemeRef keys are retained and logged without length or control-character bounds
findings.evidence: The warning path retains the entire rejected key in a process-wide dictionary and interpolates it into the diagnostic verbatim. The 256-entry cap does not bound retained bytes, and tabs and newlines are among the inputs routed to this warning. DiagnosticLog forwards the message to ETW and mirrors it to debug text. Spec 044 requires bounded payloads, and the adjacent named-style warning already bounds both retention and emission.
findings.recommendation: Apply the named-style warning's length policy, avoid retaining overlong keys, and escape control characters in the displayed identifier.

findings.title: The styling guide promises layering over author Styles the implementation cannot wrap

findings.title: Rows focused after a reorder can still be pinned at stale indices
findings.evidence: The post-move check stops if no repeater child has focus or if the focused child's index still matches. Only the index-collision branch installs a viewport watch. Reorder while focus is outside the list, then focus a shifted row, scroll it out of view, and scroll back: there is no new collection change to schedule a check, so WinUI can still return that pinned control for its old slot.
findings.recommendation: Keep stale-index monitoring active while affected containers survive. Re-arm the viewport check when focus enters an affected row, and add a selftest that focuses the row only after the reorder has settled.

findings.title: A stale index without a collision can steal focus from a correctly displayed row
findings.evidence: The check treats the absence of an index collision as proof that the focused control is serving the wrong slot. For an on-screen move from [A, B, C, D] to [D, A, B, C], B can still be correctly laid out in slot 2 while reporting its old index 1. None of the other controls needs to report 1, so the check moves focus away from B even though it never entered the pinned pool.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish a control still arranged for its own item from one reclaimed from the pinned pool; do not infer that distinction from index collisions alone. Assert focus stays on a shifted middle row after a multi-position move.

findings.title: A stale row stays pinned if no other row can take focus
findings.evidence: Focus is attempted only on other realized row controls. If the focused row contains the list's only button and the remaining rows are plain text, all candidates refuse focus. The method then returns with focus still pinning the stale control and no follow-up check. Removing that button row while scrolled away can therefore still show the deleted row on return.
findings.recommendation: Provide a fallback focus target outside the stale container, such as a focusable list host or nearby control, or recover the stale container without depending on another item accepting focus. Cover a list with just one focusable row.

findings.title: The on-screen swap test does not verify that focus survives the swap
findings.evidence: The swap-then-scroll scenario checks that initial focus was taken, but the checks after Change only inspect focus when ChangeWhileScrolledAway is true. This scenario then scrolls away and back before checking painted labels. A version that moves focus immediately on every mismatch and never installs the viewport watch could still pass it.
findings.recommendation: Assert that the original button still owns focus after the swap and before scrolling. Keep the final painted-row assertion to verify recovery after the row leaves the viewport.

findings.title: Spec 042 describes incompatible repeater lookup and animation behavior
findings.evidence: The spec first says RefreshRealizedItems iterates repeater indices, then says the keyed path never asks the repeater by index. The caller summary also promises that the right containers animate, contradicting the newly documented limitation.
findings.recommendation: Replace the obsolete refresh description, scope the no-index-lookup claim to keyed content reconciliation, and qualify the animation guarantee in the caller summary.

findings.title: Reference equality on AnimationExtras causes unchanged .ScrollLinked() and fluent implicit-transition elements to re-apply compositor/XAML animations on every render
findings.evidence: `Element.ShallowEquals` (`src/Reactor/Core/Element.cs:519`) delegates directly to synthesized `AnimationExtras.Equals` (`Element.cs:1817-1829`), where `ScrollAnimationConfig.Expressions` (`ScrollExpression[]`) and `ImplicitTransitions` properties (`ScalarTransition`, `Vector3Transition`, `BrushTransition`) use reference equality. Standard fluent modifiers in `src/Reactor/Elements/ElementExtensions.cs` unconditionally allocate fresh instances on every call: `.ScrollLinked(scrollViewer, configure)` (`ElementExtensions.cs:3335-3342`) allocates a new `ScrollExpression[]` via `builder.Build()`, and `.OpacityTransition()`, `.RotationTransition()`, `.BackgroundTransition()`, and default `.ScaleTransition()`/`.TranslationTransition()` (`ElementExtensions.cs:2711-2760`) allocate new `ScalarTransition`/`BrushTransition`/`Vector3Transition` instances. Previously, `ShallowEquals` returned `true` when such an element's own properties were unchanged. After this diff, every unrelated parent re-render declines `ShallowEquals`/`CanSkipUpdate` and enters `Reconciler.Update`: for `.ScrollLinked()`, `ApplyScrollAnimation` (`src/Reactor/Core/Reconciler.cs:6383-6397`) has no change guard (unlike `ApplyKeyframeAnimations`'s `_keyframeTriggerValues`) and allocates new `ExpressionAnimation`s and calls `visual.StartAnimation(expr.Property, animation)` on every reconcile; for `.OpacityTransition(...)`, `ApplyTransitions` (`Reconciler.cs:5559, 5615-5648`) replaces `uie.OpacityTransition` or `visual.ImplicitAnimations["Opacity"]` on every render, including while a transition is mid-flight.

findings.title: Animation guide inaccurately implies callers can avoid fresh objects/arrays with .OpacityTransition(), .Keyframes(), and .ScrollLinked()
findings.evidence: Both `docs/_pipeline/templates/animation.md.dt:46-50` and compiled `docs/guide/animation.md:33-37` state: "Native objects and arrays use reference equality: rebuilding `.OpacityTransition()`, `.WithTransitions()`, `.Keyframes()`, or `.ScrollLinked()` with fresh objects or arrays prevents skipping, even when the settings match." In `src/Reactor/Elements/ElementExtensions.cs`, `.WithTransitions(params Transition[])` (line 2696, along with `.ScaleTransition(Vector3Transition?)` and `.TranslationTransition(Vector3Transition?)` at lines 2731-2739) accepts caller-cached instances, so avoiding fresh allocations preserves skipping. By contrast, `.OpacityTransition(TimeSpan? duration = null)` (line 2711), `.Keyframes(string, object?, Func<KeyframeBuilder, KeyframeBuilder>)` (line 3314), and `.ScrollLinked(ScrollViewer, Func<ScrollAnimationBuilder, ScrollAnimationBuilder>)` (line 3335) have no overloads accepting prebuilt transitions or arrays—they unconditionally allocate `new ScalarTransition()`, `KeyframeDef[]`/`KeyframeEntry[]`, and `ScrollExpression[]` internally on every call (and `.Keyframes()`/`.ScrollLinked()` store plain managed records in arrays, not native objects). Even the PR's own tests (`AnimationExtrasEqualityTests.cs:76-90`, `AnimateModifierTests.cs:200-202`) had to bypass those fluent methods with `with { ... }` initializers to hit the skip path.
findings.recommendation: Update `docs/_pipeline/templates/animation.md.dt:46-50` and recompile `docs/guide/animation.md` (unless `ShallowEquals` is updated to structurally compare `KeyframeAnimations`/`ScrollAnimation`) so the prose distinguishes modifiers that accept reusable native instances/arrays (`.WithTransitions(cached)`, `.ItemContainerTransitions(cached)`, `.ScaleTransition(cached)`, `.TranslationTransition(cached)`) from fluent builders that always allocate per call (`.OpacityTransition()`, `.RotationTransition()`, `.BackgroundTransition()`, `.Keyframes()`, `.ScrollLinked()`) and therefore do not skip unless the whole `Element` (e.g., via `Memo`) or `ElementExtras` property is reused.
